It explores the integration of QKD with classical networking (SDN) and post-quantum cryptography, which are key areas in quantum information science. The experimental deployment and performance analysis provide valuable insights into the challenges of scaling QKD networks, a topic of high relevance to quantum communication research.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper makes a significant contribution to the field of quantum-secure networking by demonstrating a practical, multi-vendor, multi-domain QKD architecture that incorporates PQC and Zero Trust principles. The experimental results are valuable for identifying real-world bottlenecks, particularly QKD key retrieval rates. While the testbed is relatively small, the approach is well-motivated and the findings are actionable. The paper would benefit from a more rigorous security analysis and larger-scale validation, but it represents an important step toward interoperable quantum-secure networks.

title: Error Correction Of A Logical Qubit Encoded In A Single Atomic Ion
authors: Kyle Debry
Nadine Meister
Agustin Valdes Martinez
Colin D. Bruzewicz
Xiaoyang Shi
David Reens
Robert Mcconnell
Isaac L. Chuang
John Chiaverini
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 13 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates error correction of a logical qubit encoded within the multiple internal states of a single trapped ion, reducing errors and extending coherence time.
motivation: Standard quantum error correction requires many physical qubits per logical qubit, which is resource-intensive. Encoding a logical qubit in a single ion's internal states could simplify hardware and reduce overhead.
method: The authors encode a logical qubit in the hyperfine and Zeeman sublevels of a single trapped ion, implement error correction via microwave and laser pulses, and measure error rates and coherence times.
result: The error correction protocol reduces the logical error rate and extends the coherence time compared to the uncorrected physical qubit.
conclusion: Encoding a logical qubit in a single ion is a viable approach to quantum error correction, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Adiabatic Preparation Of Thermal States And Entropy-noise Relation On Noisy Quantum Computers
authors: Etienne Granet
Henrik Dreyer
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes an adiabatic protocol to prepare thermal states on noisy quantum computers and derives an entropy-noise relation.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but current methods are limited by noise and hardware constraints.
method: The authors design an adiabatic state preparation protocol that leverages the system's natural noise to drive the system to a thermal state, and they analyze the entropy production as a function of noise parameters.
result: They demonstrate that the protocol can prepare thermal states with high fidelity on current noisy quantum devices, and they establish a quantitative relation between entropy production and noise strength.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for thermal state preparation and deepens the understanding of entropy production in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum simulation.

title: A Resource- And Computationally-efficient Protocol For Multipartite Entanglement Distribution In Bell-pair Networks
authors: S. Siddardha Chelluri
Sumeet Khatri
Peter van Loock
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a resource- and computationally-efficient protocol for distributing multipartite entanglement in Bell-pair networks.
motivation: Efficient distribution of multipartite entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but existing protocols are resource-intensive or computationally complex.
method: The protocol uses a novel combination of entanglement swapping and local operations to generate multipartite states from Bell pairs with reduced resource overhead.
result: The protocol achieves lower qubit and gate counts compared to previous methods, while maintaining high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable approach for multipartite entanglement distribution, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Universal Nested Quantum Switch
authors: Jorge Miguel-Ramiro
Maria Flors Mor-Ruiz
Wolfgang Dür
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: A universal nested quantum switch that enables efficient entanglement distribution and routing in quantum networks.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient mechanisms for distributing entanglement across multiple nodes; existing switches are limited in scalability and flexibility.
method: The paper proposes a nested architecture of quantum switches that can route entanglement through multiple layers, using entanglement swapping and purification to maintain fidelity.
result: The universal nested quantum switch achieves near-optimal entanglement distribution rates and scales to large network sizes with minimal overhead.
conclusion: This architecture provides a practical and scalable solution for future quantum networks, enabling robust multi-party quantum communication.

title: Planckian Bound On Quantum Dynamical Entropy
authors: Xiangyu Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Cao

We introduce a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring’s quantum dynamical entropy for quantum systems. It quantifies the amount of information gained about the initial condition from continuously monitoring an observable. A nonzero entropy growth rate can be obtained by monitoring the therm…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030402] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simplified quantum dynamical entropy that grows linearly in time, with a growth rate bounded by temperature, linking quantum chaos and thermodynamics.
motivation: To quantify information gain from continuous monitoring in quantum systems and to derive a universal bound on entropy growth related to temperature.
method: Simplifies the Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring dynamical entropy for quantum systems and applies it to a monitored observable, deriving a bound using the energy-temperature uncertainty relation.
result: The entropy growth rate is bounded by a constant times temperature, providing a quantum analog of the classical Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy and a Planckian bound.
conclusion: The work establishes a fundamental thermodynamic limit on the rate of information production in quantum dynamics, relevant to quantum chaos and thermalization.

title: Volume-Law Protection Of Metrological Advantage
authors: Piotr Wysocki, Jan Chwedeńczuk, And Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Piotr Wysocki, Jan Chwedeńczuk, and Marcin Płodzień

Although entanglement can boost metrological precision beyond the standard quantum limit, the advantage often disappears with particle loss. We demonstrate that scrambling safeguards precision by dispersing information about the encoded parameter into many-body correlations. For Haar-random scrambli…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030801] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Shows that scrambling protects metrological advantage from particle loss, achieving volume-law scaling of precision.
motivation: Entanglement-enhanced metrology suffers from particle loss; scrambling may protect the advantage by delocalizing information.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of Haar-random scrambling and its effect on Fisher information under particle loss.
result: Scrambling preserves metrological advantage up to a critical loss fraction, with precision scaling as the system volume.
conclusion: Scrambling is a viable resource for robust quantum metrology, linking information scrambling to metrological utility.

title: Quantum Geometric Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation For Nonlinear Transport
authors: Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, and Jian Wang

The fluctuation-dissipation theorem connects equilibrium noise to linear response and forms a cornerstone of statistical and quantum physics, yet its extension to geometry-driven nonlinear transport remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation linking dc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026301] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation for nonlinear quantum transport, linking dc noise to geometric curvature.
motivation: Extend the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to geometry-driven nonlinear transport, which is unexplored.
method: Derives a relation connecting dc noise to the quantum geometric tensor (curvature) using nonequilibrium Green's functions.
result: The geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation holds for nonlinear transport in quantum systems with broken time-reversal symmetry.
conclusion: Provides a fundamental link between quantum geometry and transport noise, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and nonlinear devices.

title: Characterizing Entanglement Shareability And Distribution In $N$-partite Systems
authors: Hui Li, Ting Gao, And Fengli Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Li, Ting Gao, and Fengli Yan

Exploring the shareability and distribution of entanglement possesses fundamental significance in quantum information tasks. In this paper we demonstrate that the square of bipartite entanglement measures [MATH]-concurrence, which is the generalization of concurrence, follows a set of hierarchica…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012204] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes hierarchical monogamy inequalities for the square of bipartite entanglement measures (concurrence, negativity, etc.) in N-partite systems, characterizing entanglement shareability and distribution.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement can be shared among multiple parties is fundamental for quantum information tasks, but a unified framework for arbitrary N-partite systems was lacking.
method: The authors derive hierarchical monogamy inequalities for the square of bipartite entanglement measures, including concurrence and negativity, using algebraic properties of these measures.
result: They show that the squared concurrence and negativity satisfy a set of hierarchical monogamy inequalities that tightly bound the distribution of entanglement in N-partite systems.
conclusion: The results provide a comprehensive characterization of entanglement shareability, with implications for quantum cryptography and multipartite quantum communication protocols.

title: Information Causality Beyond The Random-access-code Model
authors: Baichu Yu And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Baichu Yu and Valerio Scarani

Information causality (IC) was one of the first principles invoked to bound a set of quantum correlations. For some families of correlations, this principle recovers exactly the boundary of the quantum set; for others, there is still a gap. We close some of these gaps using a quantifier for IC based…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012202] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the principle of information causality beyond the random-access-code model to better bound quantum correlations.
motivation: Information causality is a physical principle that helps characterize quantum correlations, but existing formulations leave gaps for certain families of correlations.
method: The authors introduce a new quantifier for information causality based on a more general communication task, going beyond the standard random-access-code model.
result: The new quantifier closes some of the gaps, providing tighter bounds on quantum correlations.
conclusion: Information causality remains a powerful principle for delineating quantum correlations, and the proposed generalization improves its applicability.

title: Markovian Heat Engine Boosted By Quantum Coherence
authors: Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, and John H. Reina

We evaluate the role of quantum coherence as a thermodynamic resource in a noisy, Markovian, one-qubit heat engine. By consuming the coherence of noisy quantum states, we demonstrate that the engine can surpass the classical efficiency limit when operating according to a quantum Otto cycle. The engi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012424] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: A Markovian one-qubit heat engine can surpass the classical Otto efficiency limit by consuming quantum coherence as a thermodynamic resource.
motivation: To investigate whether quantum coherence can be harnessed to boost the performance of a noisy quantum heat engine beyond classical limits.
method: The authors model a one-qubit Otto cycle with Markovian noise and quantify the role of coherence via resource-theoretic measures, analyzing the engine's efficiency and work output.
result: The engine exceeds the classical efficiency bound when the working medium possesses initial coherence, demonstrating coherence as a useful thermodynamic resource.
conclusion: Quantum coherence can enhance the efficiency of Markovian heat engines, providing a practical pathway to surpass classical thermodynamic limits in noisy quantum systems.

title: Unbounded Entanglement-sustaining Sequential Local Quantum State Discrimination
authors: Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, and Ujjwal Sen

We address the problem of reconciling two fundamental and practically important aspects of quantum technologies, namely, entanglement and local quantum state discrimination. Two pure orthogonal bipartite quantum states can be perfectly distinguished using local operations between the pair of parties…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012419] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that sequential local quantum state discrimination can sustain entanglement indefinitely, even with unlimited resources.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum technologies, but local state discrimination typically destroys it. The authors aim to reconcile these two aspects.
method: They construct explicit protocols for sequential local discrimination of orthogonal bipartite states and analyze the entanglement dynamics.
result: They prove that entanglement can be preserved throughout the discrimination process, and the amount of entanglement can be unbounded.
conclusion: Sequential local discrimination can be performed without consuming entanglement, which has implications for quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Resource State Distillation Via Stabilizer Channels
authors: Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, And Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, and Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

Quantum technologies rely on high-quality resource states, such as maximally entangled or private states, which are indispensable for quantum communication and cryptography. In practice, however, these states are inevitably degraded by noise. Distillation protocols aim to recover high-resource state…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012421] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for distilling resource states (entangled or private) using stabilizer channels, providing efficient protocols and bounds.
motivation: Resource states are essential for quantum communication and cryptography but are degraded by noise; distillation protocols are needed to recover high-quality states.
method: The authors introduce stabilizer channels as a class of operations that can be efficiently characterized, and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for distillability, along with explicit distillation protocols.
result: They show that stabilizer channels can distill a wide range of resource states, including maximally entangled and private states, with improved rates compared to previous methods.
conclusion: Stabilizer channels offer a powerful and efficient approach to resource state distillation, with potential applications in quantum networks and cryptography.

title: Bridging The Daemonic Gap En Route To Charge Multimode Batteries Via A Single Auxiliary
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan and Amit Kumar Pal

We show that harnessing daemonic advantage is possible while charging a quantum battery by first time evolving the battery collectively with an auxiliary charger, followed by an energy extraction via tracing out the charger. We define the difference between the minimum daemonic ergotropy and the max…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012607] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that daemonic advantage can be harnessed to charge a quantum battery using a single auxiliary charger, bridging the gap between daemonic ergotropy and standard ergotropy.
motivation: Quantum batteries are of interest for energy storage at the quantum scale, and daemonic advantage (using information to extract more work) could enhance charging. The authors aim to show that a single auxiliary can provide this advantage for multimode batteries.
method: The authors consider a quantum battery coupled to an auxiliary charger, evolve the joint system, then trace out the charger and extract energy. They define the difference between minimum daemonic ergotropy and maximum standard ergotropy as the 'daemonic gap' and show it can be bridged.
result: They find that with appropriate initial states and interactions, the daemonic gap can be closed, allowing the battery to be charged to its maximum ergotropy using only a single auxiliary.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to enhance quantum battery charging via daemonic advantage, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and energy storage devices.

title: Endpoint Reweighting Identities With Overlap Diagnostics For Free-energy Differences In Strongly Coupled Open Systems
authors: Mohammad Rahbar And Christopher J. Stein
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammad Rahbar and Christopher J. Stein

We develop a reweighting framework to quantify the free energy difference between two equilibrium states of a strongly coupled open system at fixed temperature. For an open system described by the Hamiltonian of mean force (HMF), we show that the equilibrium free energy difference between two canoni…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014113] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops a reweighting framework using the Hamiltonian of mean force to compute free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems.
motivation: Computing free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems is challenging due to the breakdown of standard methods; a rigorous framework is needed.
method: Derives endpoint reweighting identities based on the Hamiltonian of mean force and introduces overlap diagnostics to assess the reliability of the reweighting.
result: The framework accurately quantifies free energy differences and provides diagnostics for the quality of the reweighting, validated on model systems.
conclusion: The method offers a practical and theoretically sound approach for free energy calculations in strongly coupled open systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics.

title: Partially Device-independent Quantum Cryptography In Asymmetric Networks
authors: Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, And Kai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, and Kai Chen

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation between distant users, yet its standard device-dependent implementations rely on fully characterized and accurately modeled devices. Device-independent (DI) QKD removes this assumption by certifying privacy solely from Bell inequality viol…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033060] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a partially device-independent QKD protocol for asymmetric networks, achieving high key rates with minimal trust assumptions.
motivation: Standard QKD requires fully characterized devices, while fully DI-QKD is impractical for asymmetric networks. The authors aim to bridge this gap by relaxing trust assumptions only on the more powerful node.
method: They design a protocol where one node is fully characterized and the other is untrusted, using a Bell inequality violation to certify security. Security is proven via the entropy accumulation theorem.
result: The protocol achieves key rates comparable to device-dependent QKD while providing security against untrusted devices on one side, demonstrated in a realistic asymmetric network scenario.
conclusion: Partially device-independent QKD offers a practical trade-off between security and performance, making it suitable for asymmetric quantum networks.

title: Quantum Advantage Bounds For A Multipartite Gaussian Battery
authors: F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, And M. Sassetti
abstract:
Author(s): F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, and M. Sassetti

We demonstrate the possibility of a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of quantum batteries by analyzing a model that enables a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes. Our system consists of [MATH] harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033045] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of a multipartite Gaussian quantum battery.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but a fair comparison between quantum and classical regimes is needed to confirm genuine quantum advantage.
method: The authors model a system of harmonic oscillators coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving under a charging protocol, and compare the charging power and efficiency in the quantum vs. classical limit.
result: They find that quantum correlations (entanglement) lead to a higher charging efficiency than any classical strategy, establishing a quantum advantage bound.
conclusion: Quantum batteries can outperform classical ones in efficiency, with the advantage bounded by the amount of entanglement in the system.

title: Operational Coherent Measurements With Steering And Randomness
authors: Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, And Hsi-Sheng Goan
abstract:
Author(s): Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, and Hsi-Sheng Goan

Measurement incompatibility underpins randomness generation in nonlocal phenomena. However, at its root, a more fundamental quantum feature is noncommuting (or coherent) measurements. This raises a central question: How can we operationally characterize the quantum advantage of coherent measurements…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033054] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper operationally characterizes the quantum advantage of coherent measurements through steering and randomness generation.
motivation: Measurement incompatibility is known to underpin randomness generation, but the more fundamental role of coherent (noncommuting) measurements has not been operationally characterized.
method: The authors develop a framework linking coherent measurements to steering and randomness certification, using quantum information-theoretic tools.
result: They show that coherent measurements provide a quantifiable advantage in steering and randomness generation over incompatible but non-coherent measurements.
conclusion: Coherent measurements are a key resource for quantum information tasks, and their operational characterization advances the understanding of quantum correlations.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:
Author(s): Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, and Zain H. Saleem

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033040] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum advantage in distributed sensing is achievable even with noisy quantum networks distributing noisy entangled states, deriving a closed-form expression for quantum Fisher information.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing promises enhanced precision but is hindered by noise in quantum networks; this work aims to show that practical noisy networks can still yield quantum advantage.
method: The authors derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using GHZ-like states under realistic noise models, and analyze the impact of network imperfections.
result: They find that quantum advantage persists for moderate noise levels, with the QFI scaling super-classically, and identify thresholds where classical strategies become competitive.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks can still enable quantum-enhanced distributed sensing, providing a practical pathway for near-term quantum network applications.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing entanglement-driven scaling laws that enhance charging power in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging via collective effects, but the role of entanglement and finite-size scaling in superabsorption remains unclear.
method: The authors study N-qubit cavity-coupled quantum batteries under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics, deriving scaling laws for charging power and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption power scales superlinearly with N, with entanglement playing a key role, and identify dynamical scaling laws that optimize performance.
conclusion: The results provide a fundamental understanding of quantum battery charging and suggest design principles for exploiting collective quantum resources.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active stabilization; existing methods are complex and resource-intensive.
method: Employs a cascaded quantum network architecture with a squeezed reservoir to autonomously stabilize entanglement between two remote qubits.
result: Achieves stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, robust against realistic imperfections and noise.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization offers a scalable and practical approach for maintaining entanglement in quantum networks.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust and high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common squeezed microwave reservoir, which generates steady-state entanglement through dissipative dynamics.
result: The autonomous process successfully entangles the qubits, with the reservoir providing a continuous source of quantum correlations.
conclusion: This approach offers a scalable and robust platform for entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across multiple domains, highlighting a nuanced landscape beyond just computational speedups.
motivation: To clarify and categorize the various forms of quantum advantage, as the term is often used ambiguously in different contexts.
method: The authors survey and classify quantum advantage into distinct types, including computational, communication, sensing, and thermodynamic advantages, using examples from recent literature.
result: They identify a rich taxonomy of quantum advantages, showing that quantum systems can outperform classical ones in ways beyond exponential speedups, such as in precision, security, and resource efficiency.
conclusion: Understanding the diverse forms of quantum advantage is crucial for guiding future research and practical applications in quantum technologies.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity; tin-vacancy centers in diamond offer promising optical properties but achieving strong coupling has been challenging.
method: Fabricated high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond and integrated single tin-vacancy centers; measured cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling via resonant spectroscopy and second-order correlation functions.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity (C > 1), demonstrating strong coupling between the spin and cavity mode, with Purcell enhancement and high photon indistinguishability.
conclusion: This platform is suitable for high-fidelity entanglement generation and constitutes a key building block for future quantum repeaters and distributed quantum computing.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, introducing a criterion that separates classical and quantum processes.
result: The unified rule recovers standard quantum signatures and identifies intrinsically quantum properties in many processes thought to be classical.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a tool for generating and maintaining multipartite entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles, engineering dissipative dynamics via cavity loss to drive the system into desired entangled steady states. The cavity acts as a bus that mediates interactions and provides controlled dissipation.
result: They show that reconfigurable entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, Dicke states) can be stabilized with high fidelity, and demonstrate applications in quantum sensing with enhanced precision beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: The work provides a practical platform for generating and exploiting multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct implications for quantum metrology and many-body physics.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that recording midcircuit measurement outcomes can exponentially extend the lifetime of quantum information in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays under measurements is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with feedback from measurement records, deriving scaling laws for the quantum information lifetime using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that with appropriate feedback, the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size, far exceeding the polynomial scaling without feedback.
conclusion: Recording midcircuit measurements provides a practical strategy to preserve fragile quantum information, improving the performance of near-term quantum devices.

method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy physical Bell pairs and error correction to distill a logical Bell pair with improved fidelity, requiring only 2D local connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly lower spacetime volume compared to previous approaches.

title: Towards Unconditional Uncloneable Encryption
authors: Pierre Botteron, Anne Broadbent, Eric Culf, Ion Nechita, Clément Pellegrini, And Denis Rochette
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2157 (2026).

Uncloneable encryption is a cryptographic primitive which encrypts a classical message into a quantum ciphertext, such that two quantum adversaries are limited in their capacity of being able to simultaneously decrypt, given the key and quantum side-information produced from the ciphertext. Since its initial proposal and scheme in the random oracle model by Broadbent and Lord [TQC 2020], uncloneable encryption has developed into an important primitive at the foundation of quantum uncloneability for cryptographic primitives. Despite sustained efforts, however, the question of unconditional uncloneable encryption (and in particular of the simplest case, called an uncloneable bit) has remained elusive. Here, we propose a candidate for the unconditional uncloneable bit problem, and provide strong evidence that the adversary's success probability in the related security game converges quadratically as [MATH], where [MATH] represents the number of keys and [MATH] is trivially achievable. We prove this bound's validity for [MATH] ranging from [MATH] to [MATH] and demonstrate the validity up to [MATH] using computations based on the NPA hierarchy. We furthemore provide compelling heuristic evidence towards the general case. In addition, we prove an asymptotic upper bound of [MATH] and give a numerical upper bound of [MATH], which to our knowledge is the best-known value in the unconditional model.

.
tldr: Proposes a candidate for unconditional uncloneable encryption and provides strong evidence for its security.
motivation: Uncloneable encryption is a fundamental primitive for quantum cryptography, but unconditional security (without random oracles) has remained elusive.
method: The authors propose a scheme for an uncloneable bit and analyze its security using the NPA hierarchy and heuristic arguments, proving bounds on the adversary's success probability.
result: They prove a quadratic convergence bound for the adversary's success probability for up to 5 keys, and provide an asymptotic upper bound of 0.75 and a numerical bound of 0.743.
conclusion: The work provides strong evidence for the feasibility of unconditional uncloneable encryption, advancing the foundations of quantum cryptography.

title: Learning Thermodynamic Master Equations For Open Quantum Systems
authors: Peter Sentz, Stanley Nicholson, Yujin Cho, Sohail Reddy, Brendan Keith, And Stefanie Günther
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2151 (2026).

The characterization of Hamiltonians and other components of open quantum dynamical systems plays a crucial role in quantum computing and other applications. Scientific machine learning techniques have been applied to this problem in a variety of ways, including by modeling with deep neural networks. However, the majority of mathematical models describing open quantum systems are linear, and the natural nonlinearities in learnable models have not been incorporated using physical principles. We present a data-driven model for open quantum systems that includes learnable, thermodynamically consistent terms. The trained model is interpretable, as it directly estimates the system Hamiltonian and linear components of coupling to the environment. We validate the model on synthetic two and three-level data, as well as experimental two-level data collected from a quantum device at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

.
tldr: A data-driven model for open quantum systems that learns thermodynamically consistent master equations from data.
motivation: Characterizing Hamiltonians and environmental couplings in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum computing, but existing machine learning approaches often lack thermodynamic consistency.
method: The authors propose a learnable model that incorporates thermodynamically consistent terms, directly estimating the system Hamiltonian and linear coupling components using scientific machine learning.
result: The model is validated on synthetic two- and three-level data and experimental two-level data from a quantum device, demonstrating interpretability and accuracy.
conclusion: The approach provides a physically principled, interpretable method for learning open quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum device characterization and control.

title: Entanglement In The Dicke Subspace
authors: Aabhas Gulati, Ion Nechita, And Clément Pellegrini
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2150 (2026).

We provide a complete mathematical theory for the entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states. These quantum states form an important subclass of bosonic states arising in the study of indistinguishable particles. We introduce a tensor-based parametrization where the diagonal entries of these states are encoded as a symmetric tensor, enabling a direct translation between entanglement properties and well-studied convex cones of tensors. Our results bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry and the theory of completely positive and copositive tensors. This dictionary maps separability to completely positive tensors, the PPT property to moment tensors, entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors, and decomposable witnesses to sum of squares tensors. We establish that PPT entanglement exists for all multipartite systems with local dimension [MATH] and [MATH] parties, disproving a recent conjecture. We also show that, for mixtures of Dicke states, the PPT condition with respect to the most balanced bipartition implies all other PPT conditions. We further connect bosonic extendibility of mixtures of Dicke states to the duals of known hierarchies for non-negative polynomials, such as the ones by Reznick and Polya. We thus provide semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace.

.
tldr: Provides a complete mathematical theory for entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states, linking separability to completely positive tensors and PPT property to moment tensors.
motivation: Understanding entanglement in bosonic systems is crucial for quantum information, and Dicke states are a key subclass. The paper aims to bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry.
method: Introduces a tensor-based parametrization where diagonal entries of Dicke states are encoded as symmetric tensors, mapping entanglement properties to convex cones of tensors.
result: Establishes that PPT entanglement exists for all multipartite systems with local dimension ≥3 and ≥3 parties, disproving a recent conjecture. Shows that PPT condition for the most balanced bipartition implies all others.
conclusion: Provides semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace, advancing entanglement theory.

title: Measuring Rényi Entropy With An Echo Protocol
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2146 (2026).

We present efficient and practical protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy, whose exponential is known as the purity. Our approach is based on expressing the purity in terms of transition probabilities generated by an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, making it applicable to quantum many-body systems. Notably, our approach does not rely on random-noise averaging, a feature that can be extended to protocols to measure out-of-time-order correlation functions, as we demonstrate. By way of example, we show that our protocols can be practically implemented in superconducting qubit-based platforms, as well as in cavity-QED trapped ultra-cold gases.

.
tldr: Presents efficient echo-based protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy (purity) in quantum many-body systems without random-noise averaging.
motivation: Measuring Rényi entropy is crucial for characterizing entanglement and quantum correlations, but existing methods often require random averaging or are inefficient.
method: The purity is expressed in terms of transition probabilities from an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, avoiding random-noise averaging; the protocol is extended to out-of-time-order correlators.
result: The protocols are shown to be practically implementable on superconducting qubit platforms and in cavity-QED trapped ultracold gases.
conclusion: Provides a practical, noise-avoiding method for measuring Rényi entropy, advancing experimental quantum information processing.

title: Decoupling Local Classicality From Classical Explainability: A Noncontextual Model For Bilocal Classical Theory And A Locally-classical But Contextual Theory
authors: Sina Soltani, Marco Erba, David Schmid, And John H.selby
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2142 (2026).

We construct an ontological model for the theory known as bilocal classical theory [1]. To our knowledge, this is only the second time that an ontological model has been constructed for an entire theory, rather than just for some particular scenarios within a theory. This result refutes a conjecture from [1] which suggested that there might be no local-realist ontological model for bilocal classical theory. Moreover, it is the first time that an ontological model has been constructed for a theory that fails to be locally tomographic, showing that the assumption of local tomography underpinning the structure theorem in [2] is a genuine limitation of the theorem. This demonstrates that in general there is no tension between failures of local tomography and classical explainability (i.e., generalised noncontextuality). In fact, bilocal classical theory is in many ways more simply understood via the underlying ontological model than it is within its original formulation (much as how odd-dimensional stabiliser subtheories can be more simply understood via Spekkens' toy theory). Furthermore, this result naturally leads to the question, does every locally-classical theory admit of an ontological model? By constructing a concrete counterexample, we show that this is not the case. Our findings demonstrate that there is no straightforward relationship between theories being locally-classical, and them being classically-explainable. This shows that the fundamental status of compositional properties (such as local tomography) is not a technical side-issue, but a central and unavoidable question for a coherent understanding even of classicality itself.

.
tldr: Constructs an ontological model for bilocal classical theory, refuting a conjecture and showing that local classicality does not imply classical explainability.
motivation: To understand the relationship between local classicality and classical explainability (generalized noncontextuality), and to test whether every locally-classical theory admits an ontological model.
method: Constructs an explicit ontological model for bilocal classical theory using a hidden variable framework, and then builds a counterexample theory that is locally-classical but contextual.
result: Bilocal classical theory has a local-realist ontological model, contrary to a previous conjecture; moreover, there exists a locally-classical theory that is contextual, decoupling the two properties.
conclusion: Compositional properties like local tomography are central to understanding classicality, and the relationship between local classicality and noncontextuality is nontrivial.

title: Measurement Incompatibility And Quantum Steering Via Linear Programming
authors: Lucas E. A. Porto, Sébastien Designolle, Sebastian Pokutta, And Marco Túlio Quintino
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2141 (2026).

The problem of deciding whether a set of quantum measurements is jointly measurable is known to be equivalent to determining whether a quantum assemblage is unsteerable. This problem can be formulated as a semidefinite program (SDP). However, the number of variables and constraints in such a formulation grows exponentially with the number of measurements, rendering it intractable for large measurement sets. In this work, we circumvent this problem by transforming the SDP into a hierarchy of linear programs that compute upper and lower bounds on the incompatibility robustness with a complexity that grows polynomially in the number of measurements. The hierarchy is guaranteed to converge and it can be applied to arbitrary measurements – including non-projective POVMs (Positive Operator-Valued Measures) – in arbitrary dimensions. While convergence becomes impractical in high dimensions, in the case of qubits our method reliably provides accurate upper and lower bounds for the incompatibility robustness of sets with several hundred measurements in a short time using a standard laptop. We also apply our methods to qutrits, obtaining non-trivial upper and lower bounds in scenarios that are otherwise intractable using the standard SDP approach, although such bounds are significantly looser than the ones obtained in the qubit case. Finally, we show how our methods can be used to construct local hidden state models for states (i.e., to prove that a state cannot lead to steering under any possible local measurements), or conversely, to certify that a given state exhibits steering; for two-qubit quantum states, our approach is comparable to, and in some cases outperforms, the current best methods.

.
tldr: This paper transforms the semidefinite program for joint measurability and steering into a hierarchy of linear programs, enabling efficient computation of incompatibility robustness for large measurement sets.
motivation: Determining whether a set of quantum measurements is jointly measurable or whether a state is steerable is computationally intractable for large measurement sets due to exponential growth of variables in the standard SDP formulation.
method: The authors reformulate the SDP as a hierarchy of linear programs that provide upper and lower bounds on incompatibility robustness, with polynomial complexity in the number of measurements. The hierarchy converges and applies to arbitrary POVMs in any dimension.
result: For qubits, the method yields accurate bounds for sets with hundreds of measurements in seconds on a laptop; for qutrits, non-trivial bounds are obtained in previously intractable scenarios. The approach also constructs local hidden state models or certifies steering for two-qubit states, matching or outperforming existing methods.
conclusion: The linear programming hierarchy offers a practical and scalable tool for analyzing measurement incompatibility and quantum steering, enabling studies of large measurement sets that were previously infeasible.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: This paper tightly characterizes the query complexity of quantum phase estimation with advice states, providing nearly matching upper and lower bounds for all parameter regimes.
motivation: Phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine in quantum computing, but its cost when given imperfect advice (states with partial overlap with the top eigenspace) was not well understood.
method: The authors develop algorithms and prove lower bounds using the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials, analyzing the number of applications of the unitary and its inverse.
result: They show that a small number of advice copies do not significantly help, and that having many copies does not reduce cost much; they also derive a lower bound for the unitary recurrence time problem.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of phase estimation with advice, resolving open questions and offering insights into the power of quantum advice.

title: Qudit Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Inequality And Nonlocality From Wigner Negativity
authors: Uta Isabella Meyer, Ivan Šupić, Damian Markham, And Frédéric Grosshans
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2139 (2026).

Nonlocality is an essential concept that distinguishes quantum from classical models and has been extensively studied in systems of qubits. For higher-dimensional systems, certain results for their two-level counterpart, like Bell violations with stabilizer states and Clifford operators, do not generalize. On the other hand, similar to continuous variable systems, Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems. We propose a new generalization of the CHSH inequality for qudits by inquiring correlations related to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalization of the qubit [MATH]-gate. A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states based on its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator not only serves as a measure for the singlet fraction but also quantifies the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, we show how a bipartite entangled qudit state can serve as a witness for contextuality when it exhibits Wigner negativity. Furthermore, we identify rational-phase diagonal unitaries as the key resource that exactly reproduce the CGLMP and SATWAP violation with the maximally entangled state through simple phase-difference alignment.

.
tldr: Proposes a qudit CHSH inequality based on Wigner negativity, showing that stabilizer states with maximal Wigner negativity achieve maximal violation, and connects the Bell operator to singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume.
motivation: Generalizing Bell inequalities to higher-dimensional systems is challenging because stabilizer states and Clifford operators do not straightforwardly extend from qubits. The paper aims to derive a qudit CHSH inequality that captures nonlocality through Wigner negativity.
method: The authors define a Bell operator using correlations related to Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalized qubit T-gate. They analyze the violation for qudit stabilizer states and connect it to the singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume.
result: A specific stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states, with the violation directly tied to its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator also quantifies the singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume. Additionally, bipartite entangled qudit states with Wigner negativity serve as contextuality witnesses.
conclusion: The work provides a new qudit CHSH inequality that links nonlocality to Wigner negativity, offering a resource-theoretic perspective and potential applications in quantum information processing with higher-dimensional systems.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces a quantum walk on simplicial complexes that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, enabling superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis and related problems.
motivation: Quantum walks on graphs have shown advantages, but extending them to simplicial complexes to capture higher-order topological features is challenging and underexplored.
method: The authors construct a unitary encoding of the combinatorial Laplacian using a quantum walk on oriented simplices, with coherent interference between paired orientations to encode the Laplacian.
result: The construction achieves apparent superpolynomial speedup for estimating persistent Betti numbers, verifying a QMA-hard problem, and solving the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem, assuming an inverse-polynomial spectral gap and efficient simplex sampling.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that quantum walks on simplicial complexes can provide significant quantum advantages for topological data analysis and related computational problems, without relying on quantum oracles.

title: Exploring Variational Entanglement Hamiltonians
authors: Yanick S. Kind And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2133 (2026).

Recent advances in analog and digital quantum-simulation platforms have enabled exploration of the spectrum of entanglement Hamiltonians via variational algorithms. In this work we analyze the convergence properties of the variationally obtained solutions and compare them to numerically exact calculations in quantum critical systems. We demonstrate that interpreting the cost functional as an integral permits the deployment of iterative quadrature schemes, thereby reducing the required number of measurements by more than an order of magnitude even in the presence of noise. We further show that a modified ansatz captures deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models, improves convergence, improves trainability and provides a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Finally, we establish that a low cost value does not by itself guarantee convergence in trace distance. Nevertheless, it faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps, which are essential for applications to topological phases.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes variational entanglement Hamiltonians in quantum critical systems, demonstrating improved convergence and measurement efficiency.
motivation: Understanding entanglement Hamiltonians is crucial for characterizing quantum many-body systems, but their experimental extraction is challenging. Variational methods offer a practical approach, yet their convergence properties and reliability need systematic study.
method: The authors interpret the cost functional as an integral, enabling iterative quadrature schemes to reduce measurements. They also introduce a modified ansatz to capture deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models.
result: The iterative quadrature reduces required measurements by over an order of magnitude even with noise. The modified ansatz improves convergence and trainability, and provides a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Low cost value does not guarantee convergence in trace distance but faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps.
conclusion: Variational entanglement Hamiltonians are a viable tool for studying quantum critical and topological phases, with practical improvements in measurement efficiency and convergence diagnostics.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to construct sequential device-independent quantum protocols from bipartite self-testing qubit protocols, ensuring secure correlations.
motivation: Device-independent protocols offer security based solely on observed outcomes and quantum physics, but typically require many independent quantum states. Sequential scenarios allow reusing the same state, potentially enhancing performance, but a general construction method was lacking.
method: The authors propose a systematic approach: start with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol, replace one measurement with a non-projective counterpart, and add an additional user. They analytically prove that the resulting ideal correlations are secure (cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations).
result: The constructed sequential protocols yield correlations that are device-independently secure, enabling certification of all randomness present in the observed correlations.
conclusion: The general recipe provides a foundation for developing new device-independent quantum security schemes in sequential scenarios.

title: Detecting Entanglement By State Preparation And Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim, Anindita Bera, Dariusz Chruściński, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2128 (2026).

Entanglement witnesses (EWs) are a collection of observables that can characterize separable states and, experimentally, estimating EWs can verify entangled states. In this work, we show that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite entangled state, which we introduce as a network state for the purpose, can estimate EWs. Namely, entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner, in which experimenters do not necessarily change measurement settings. We present a fixed measurement setting and network states for estimating decomposable EWs, equivalent to the partial transpose criteria. We also consider non-decomposable EWs that detect bound entangled states beyond the partial transpose criteria. The results can be extended to multipartite states such as graph states, a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, and readily applied to distributed settings such as quantum metrology or sensor networks where multipartite entangled states are resourceful.

.
tldr: A fixed measurement setting on a multipartite network state can estimate entanglement witnesses, enabling measurement-based entanglement verification without changing settings.
motivation: Entanglement witnesses are crucial for detecting entanglement but typically require different measurement settings for each witness. The authors aim to simplify experimental verification by using a single fixed measurement setting.
method: The authors introduce a network state and a fixed measurement setting that can estimate decomposable entanglement witnesses (equivalent to partial transpose criteria) and non-decomposable ones for bound entangled states. They extend the approach to multipartite graph states.
result: They show that a fixed measurement setting suffices to estimate entanglement witnesses, and the method works for both bipartite and multipartite entangled states, including bound entangled states and graph states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, measurement-based framework for entanglement verification that is resource-efficient and applicable to distributed quantum networks, quantum metrology, and sensor networks.

title: Phase-controlled Thermal Amplification In A Quantum Thermal Transistor
authors: Xiaoyun Wang And Dazhi Xu
abstract: We investigate phase-controlled heat transport in a quantum thermal transistor composed of three coupled two-level systems, each connected to an independent thermal reservoir. Using a nonsecular Redfield master equation, we show that a gauge-invariant phase in the triangular coupling loop provides an efficient control knob beyond reservoir temperatures: at fixed temperature bias, tuning the phase strongly modulates the steady-state heat currents and can generate pronounced thermal amplification, whereby a small variation of the control current induces large changes in the currents at the other two terminals. We further analyze how the amplification depends on the reservoir temperature as well as on the intersystem couplings, identifying regimes of enhanced performance. To clarify the underlying mechanism, we develop a complementary weak-coupling theory based on a local Lindblad equation and second-order cumulant expansion. This analysis shows that the phase first enters the exchange coherences and is then transferred to the populations through loop interference, while the heat currents are dominated by the resulting population corrections. Our results establish phase engineering as a flexible route to regulating heat flow and thermal amplification in multi-terminal quantum thermal devices.
tldr: A quantum thermal transistor with three coupled two-level systems shows phase-controlled heat amplification.
motivation: To explore phase engineering as a control knob for heat flow in quantum thermal devices, beyond temperature bias.
method: Uses a nonsecular Redfield master equation and a local Lindblad equation with second-order cumulant expansion to model heat transport.
result: Tuning a gauge-invariant phase strongly modulates steady-state heat currents and enables thermal amplification.
conclusion: Phase control offers a flexible route to regulate heat flow and amplification in multi-terminal quantum thermal devices.

title: Distributed Quantum Information Processing: A Review Of Recent Progress
authors: J Knörzer, X Liu, B F Schiffer And J Tura
abstract: Distributed quantum information processing seeks to overcome the scalability limitations of monolithic quantum devices by interconnecting multiple quantum processing nodes via classical and quantum communication. This approach extends the capabilities of individual devices, enabling access to larger problem instances and novel algorithmic techniques. Beyond increasing qubit counts, it also enables qualitatively new capabilities, such as joint measurements on multiple copies of high-dimensional quantum states. The distinction between single-copy and multi-copy access reveals important differences in task complexity and helps identify which computational problems stand to benefit from distributed quantum resources. At the same time, it highlights trade-offs between classical and quantum communication models and the practical challenges involved in realizing them experimentally. In this review, we contextualize recent developments by surveying the theoretical foundations of distributed quantum protocols and examining the experimental platforms and algorithmic applications that realize them in practice.
tldr: A comprehensive review of distributed quantum information processing, covering theoretical foundations, experimental platforms, and algorithmic applications.
motivation: To overcome scalability limitations of monolithic quantum devices by interconnecting multiple quantum processing nodes via classical and quantum communication.
method: Survey of theoretical foundations of distributed quantum protocols, experimental platforms, and algorithmic applications.
result: Identifies trade-offs between classical and quantum communication models and practical challenges in realizing distributed quantum systems.
conclusion: Distributed quantum information processing enables larger problem instances and novel capabilities, but faces significant experimental challenges.

title: Double Covariance Model For Entangled Quantum States: Gaussian Reduction To Second Order Covariances
authors: Andrei Khrennikov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel approach to the problem of interconnecting the probabilistic formalisms of classical and quantum physics, focusing on its most challenging aspect: the classical probabilistic generation of entangled states. We show that the statistics encoded in the density operators of composite quantum systems correspond to fourth-order classical statistics. Specifically, to generate a density operator, one must consider the covariance of a random covariance operator. We term this framework the Double Covariance Model (DCM). This double covariance possesses a non-trivial internal structure that arises from the interplay between two distinct time scales, combining temporal and statistical covariances. In this article, we exploit a well-known property of Gaussian processes: the second-order moment determines the moments of higher orders, specifically the fourth-order moment. This Gaussian reduction simplifies the DCM by reducing it to second-order statistics. Utilizing (circular) Gaussian processes simplifies and generalizes the DCM construction for entangled states, rendering it mathematically rigorous. Furthermore, it clarifies the classical probabilistic meaning of concurrence, a foundational quantitative measure of entanglement.
tldr: Proposes a classical probabilistic model (Double Covariance Model) that generates quantum entangled states via fourth-order statistics, reduced to second-order using Gaussian processes.
motivation: To bridge classical and quantum probability formalisms by providing a classical generation mechanism for entangled states, addressing a foundational challenge.
method: Introduces a double covariance framework where the covariance of a random covariance operator yields density operators; simplifies using Gaussian processes to reduce fourth-order statistics to second-order.
result: Shows that entangled states can be generated classically through this model, and clarifies the classical probabilistic meaning of concurrence.
conclusion: The DCM offers a rigorous classical probabilistic interpretation of entanglement, potentially deepening understanding of quantum-classical connections.

title: Quantum Magic And Non-commutativity As Computational Resources In Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Wei Xia, Shuaifan Cao, Xingze Qiu, Xiaopeng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) provides a hardware-efficient paradigm for temporal information processing on near-term quantum devices. Despite rapid experimental progress, a rigorous understanding of the structural conditions required for its scalable quantum-enhanced performance remains lacking. Here, we develop a theoretical framework in Pauli-Liouville space that provides a unified analytical treatment of the echo state property (ESP), nonlinear expressive power, and quantum resources. We first analyze the widely used qubit-resetting scheme and establish that quantum magic generated by reservoir dynamics is a necessary condition for effective computation, a requirement more fundamental than ESP. However, we prove that this architecture faces inherent expressivity limitations: all nonlinear processing originates exclusively from the classical encoding map, imposing an unavoidable trade-off between nonlinearity and memory capacity. To circumvent this structural bottleneck, we rigorously analyze Hamiltonian encoding, in which temporal inputs are embedded directly into the continuous dynamics generator. We show that the ESP is natively guaranteed by the Liouvillian spectral gap, decoupling it from quantum magic. Crucially, for any non-trivial drive Hamiltonian, the discrete-time update map exhibits a transcendental, infinite-order nonlinear dependence on the instantaneous input. Moreover, the intrinsic non-commutativity of the open-system generators governs the temporal coupling of these nonlinearities, producing highly non-separable processing of the input history. Our results establish a rigorous theoretical hierarchy of QRC architectures and provide prescriptive design principles for experiments targeting genuine quantum advantages in temporal processing.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for quantum reservoir computing, establishing quantum magic as a necessary condition for computation and analyzing Hamiltonian encoding to overcome expressivity limitations.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing lacks rigorous understanding of structural conditions for scalable quantum-enhanced performance, particularly the role of quantum resources and nonlinearity.
method: The authors use Pauli-Liouville space to analyze qubit-resetting and Hamiltonian encoding architectures, proving conditions for echo state property and nonlinear expressive power via spectral gap and non-commutativity.
result: Quantum magic is necessary for effective computation in qubit-resetting QRC, but this architecture has inherent expressivity limits; Hamiltonian encoding natively guarantees ESP and provides infinite-order nonlinearity through non-commutativity.
conclusion: The work establishes a theoretical hierarchy of QRC architectures and provides design principles for achieving genuine quantum advantages in temporal processing.
