title: Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of The Acoustoelectric Quantum Vacuum
authors: Ryan O. Behunin, Andrew Shepherd, Francesco Intravaia, Matt Eichenfield
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum vacuum can assume thermal properties as a consequence of system kinematics, highlighting the nuance of our definition of particles in quantum field theory. Here, we explore this phenomenon in acoustoelectric systems, involving the interaction of phonons and plasmons, where the charge carriers drift at a constant velocity exceeding the speed of sound. Through an open quantum systems analysis, we show that the acoustoelectric quantum vacuum acquires a thermal character with a temperature defined by the drift velocity and the phonon wavevector. Realistic parameters yield effective temperatures of several Kelvin, establishing acoustoelectric systems as a promising platform for the investigation of quantum vacuum effects.
tldr: The quantum vacuum in acoustoelectric systems acquires a thermal character due to drifting charge carriers, with effective temperatures of several Kelvin.
motivation: To explore how the quantum vacuum can exhibit thermal properties in acoustoelectric systems, where charge carriers drift faster than sound, and to establish a platform for studying quantum vacuum effects.
method: Open quantum systems analysis of phonon-plasmon interactions with drifting charge carriers, deriving the effective temperature of the acoustoelectric quantum vacuum.
result: The acoustoelectric quantum vacuum becomes thermal with temperature proportional to drift velocity and phonon wavevector; realistic parameters yield effective temperatures of several Kelvin.
conclusion: Acoustoelectric systems are a promising platform for investigating quantum vacuum effects, bridging quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics.

Using an open quantum systems approach, they analyze the interaction between phonons and plasmons and show that the acoustoelectric vacuum exhibits a temperature proportional to the drift velocity and phonon wavevector. With realistic parameters, effective temperatures of several Kelvin are predicted, making acoustoelectric systems a viable platform for studying quantum vacuum effects. abstract:
Author(s): Yiran Wang and Yongming Li

Quantum state transformations and resource reversibility in quantum resource theories have always been of interest to researchers. It is well known that quantum catalysts can enhance the capabilities of quantum state transformations. Previous studies have shown that bound magic states are asymptotic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012427] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the irreversibility of bound magic states in quantum resource theories and shows that catalysis can enhance reversibility.
motivation: Understanding resource reversibility is fundamental in quantum resource theories; bound magic states are known to be irreversible, but the role of catalysts in enabling reversibility is explored.
method: The authors analyze the transformation of bound magic states under free operations, introducing catalytic assistance and deriving conditions for reversibility.
result: They demonstrate that catalysis can make certain irreversible bound magic state transformations reversible, providing a complete characterization of catalytic reversibility.
conclusion: Catalysis can overcome the irreversibility of bound magic states, offering new insights into the structure of quantum resource theories and potential applications in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Semidefinite Programming For Understanding The Limitations Of Lindblad Equations
authors: Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, And Devashish Tupkary
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, and Devashish Tupkary

Lindbladian quantum master equations (LEs) are the most popular descriptions for quantum systems weakly coupled to baths. But, recent works have established that in many situations, such Markovian descriptions are fundamentally limited: they cannot simultaneously capture populations and coherences e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012423] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses semidefinite programming to characterize the fundamental limitations of Lindblad master equations in simultaneously describing populations and coherences.
motivation: Lindblad equations are widely used but have known limitations; the authors aim to systematically understand and quantify these limitations.
method: They formulate the problem as a semidefinite program (SDP) to find the best possible Lindblad equation that approximates a given exact dynamics, and analyze the constraints.
result: The SDP approach reveals trade-offs between accuracy in populations and coherences, providing bounds on how well Lindblad equations can capture both.
conclusion: The work offers a rigorous framework to assess the validity of Markovian approximations and guides the development of more accurate quantum master equations.

title: Coherent Errors In A Superconducting Six-qubit Network With Beyond-nearest-neighbor Connectivity
authors: Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, And R. Vijay
abstract:
Author(s): Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, and R. Vijay

Enhancing qubit connectivity in quantum processors is an important milestone for more efficient implementation of algorithms and novel error-correction protocols. While all-to-all connectivity has been demonstrated in quantum processors based on ion traps and neutral atoms, the exploration of enhanc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033049] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally characterizes coherent errors in a six-qubit superconducting processor with beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity, using randomized benchmarking and gate set tomography.
motivation: Enhancing qubit connectivity is crucial for efficient algorithm implementation and error correction, but coherent errors can limit performance; understanding them is key for scalable quantum processors.
method: The authors fabricate a six-qubit superconducting processor with a specific connectivity graph and perform randomized benchmarking and gate set tomography to characterize coherent errors in single- and two-qubit gates.
result: They identify dominant coherent error sources, such as crosstalk and residual coupling, and quantify their impact on gate fidelities, showing that beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity introduces additional error channels.
conclusion: The study provides insights into error mitigation strategies for superconducting qubit networks with enhanced connectivity, guiding future hardware design and error correction protocols.

title: Stroboscopic Saturation Of Multiparameter Quantum Limits In Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: Berihu Teklu And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Berihu Teklu and Victor Montenegro

A naturally multiparameter sensing scenario arises in spatially distributed networks of quantum sensors, where each node probes a distinct parameter of interest. In such settings, the central challenges are to achieve quantum-enhanced sensitivity under well-defined resource constraints and to explic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033053] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies multiparameter quantum sensing in distributed networks, establishing fundamental limits and showing that stroboscopic control can saturate the quantum bounds.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing networks face challenges in achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity under resource constraints, especially for multiple parameters. Understanding the fundamental limits and how to saturate them is crucial for practical quantum metrology.
method: The authors derive quantum Cramér-Rao bounds for multiparameter estimation in a distributed sensor network, and propose a stroboscopic measurement strategy that adaptively probes the parameters to achieve the optimal scaling.
result: They show that the stroboscopic protocol saturates the multiparameter quantum limits, achieving Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for each parameter simultaneously, and outperforms simultaneous or sequential strategies.
conclusion: Stroboscopic control provides a practical route to optimal multiparameter quantum sensing in distributed networks, with implications for quantum-enhanced imaging, navigation, and fundamental tests.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving immunity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-robust approach using entangled states.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic symmetry that cancels common-mode noise, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation using quantum metrology techniques.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being insensitive to common-mode fluctuations, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical and scalable path toward quantum-enhanced sensor networks, with potential applications in precision measurements and quantum sensing.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss at breakeven using continuous drives extends qubit lifetime beyond physical limits.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect against photon loss, achieving error correction at the breakeven point where the corrected qubit lifetime exceeds the uncorrected physical limit.
result: The passive scheme successfully extends the qubit lifetime past its physical limits, demonstrating error correction at breakeven without active measurements.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, posing a challenge for quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They identify a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: Mitigating radiation-induced correlated errors is essential for achieving fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as long-lived quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses defect centers with high-spin nuclei to repeatedly transfer entanglement from electron spins to nuclear spin qudits, accumulating multipartite entanglement.
result: Demonstrates that repeated entanglement transfer can generate high-dimensional entangled states between nuclear memory qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical route to implementing quantum repeaters and quantum networks with enhanced dimensionality and memory lifetimes.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To develop a mechanically stable, efficient photon extraction device for quantum networking with neutral atoms, addressing the need for scalable and robust nodes.
method: Design and fabrication of an on-chip parabolic mirror with fiber in/out coupling, integrated with neutral atoms for photon collection and routing.
result: Demonstrated efficient photon extraction and coupling, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms in a compact form factor.
conclusion: The parabolic mirror on an optical chip provides a promising platform for scalable quantum network nodes, combining efficiency and mechanical stability.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitary operations required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function negativity.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it determines the minimal number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation, the compression rate, and the number of measurement settings in tomography.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful tool for quantifying non-Gaussianity and has direct implications for resource theory and practical quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging, especially in finite magnetic fields.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve state-selective, low-loss imaging and loading of atoms in an optical tweezer array, leveraging a three-level lambda system.
result: They achieve high-fidelity (>99%) nondestructive imaging and efficient loading of atom arrays, with reduced scattering and heating compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provide a practical route to scalable neutral-atom quantum information processing, particularly for systems requiring operation in finite magnetic fields.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilizing blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To explore exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, where long-range interactions and kinetic constraints can lead to novel phenomena beyond standard cavity QED.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, incorporating kinetically constrained long-range interactions, and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating a new class of non-equilibrium phases.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for studying kinetically constrained many-body physics in cavity QED, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is often impractical; variational approximations are needed.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to systematically construct approximate counterdiabatic Hamiltonians.
result: The method yields higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving for several quantum control tasks.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise. The authors aim to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: They map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error-correcting code principles to cancel k-local noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, enabling practical suppression of spatially correlated noise in large quantum systems.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a scalable approach to noise mitigation in quantum information processing.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function gradient under noise, connecting circuit expressivity (measured by the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra) to noise resilience.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity, and provide concentration estimates that depend on noise strength and circuit structure.
conclusion: The results offer a principled guide for designing noise-resilient variational circuits and optimizing training, advancing the theory of quantum machine learning.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys CV quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) protocols, including Gaussian-modulated coherent states and discrete modulation, security proofs against collective and coherent attacks, and experimental implementations.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and rates, with security proofs now covering finite-size effects and composable security. The review also discusses measurement-device-independent and twin-field CV-QKD variants.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and rapidly advancing field, with potential for integration into quantum networks and practical deployment.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but many primitives are less known; this review organizes and assesses them.
method: The paper classifies quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, blind quantum computing) and discusses their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: It provides a comprehensive taxonomy of quantum cryptographic primitives, highlighting their security guarantees and practical limitations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but many face significant experimental and theoretical challenges before practical deployment.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with emphasis on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of universal behavior in driven open systems, guiding future experiments and theory.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To constrain possible theories of quantum gravity using quantum information methods, particularly through tabletop experiments that probe the quantum nature of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes proposed tabletop-scale experiments that would detect entanglement between two probes mediated by gravity.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified that could test the quantumness of gravity, with detailed analysis of their requirements and potential outcomes.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods provide a concrete way to test quantum gravity, and GIE experiments offer a promising near-term approach.

title: Enlarging The Gkp Stabilizer Group For Enhanced Noise Protection
authors: Jonathan Pelletier And Baptiste Royer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2156 (2026).

Encoding a qubit in a larger Hilbert space of an oscillator is an efficient way to protect its quantum information against decoherence. Promising examples of such bosonic encodings are the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. In this work, we investigate how redefining the stabilizer group of the GKP codes to include all operations with trivial action on the code space can contribute to the search for an optimal implementation of a logical circuit when it is affected by noise. We find the generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group, allowing us to search for different physical implementations of a Clifford operation. We then propose an algorithm that finds the optimal implementation of a given logical Clifford circuit on GKP codes, such that the state is less affected by loss errors during the computation. Finally, we demonstrate numerically, with logical randomized benchmarking, that such a compiler can increase the lifetime of square-GKP qubits while running Clifford circuits, compared to a random walk compiler.

.
tldr: This paper enlarges the GKP stabilizer group to include all operations with trivial action on the code space, enabling optimal implementation of logical Clifford circuits with enhanced noise protection.
motivation: GKP codes are promising for protecting quantum information in oscillators, but finding optimal physical implementations of logical circuits under noise remains challenging.
method: The authors identify the generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group and propose an algorithm that searches for the optimal implementation of a given logical Clifford circuit on GKP codes to minimize loss errors.
result: Numerical simulations using logical randomized benchmarking show that the compiler increases the lifetime of square-GKP qubits during Clifford circuits compared to a random walk compiler.
conclusion: Redefining the stabilizer group and optimizing circuit implementations can significantly improve noise protection for GKP codes, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: A Complexity Theory For Non-local Quantum Computation
authors: Andreas Bluhm, Simon Höfer, Alex May, Mikka Stasiuk, Philip Verduyn Lunel, And Henry Yuen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2152 (2026).

Non-local quantum computation (NLQC) replaces a local interaction between two systems with a single round of communication and shared entanglement. Despite many partial results, it is known that a characterization of entanglement cost in at least certain NLQC tasks would imply significant breakthroughs in complexity theory. Here, we avoid these obstructions and take an indirect approach to understanding resource requirements in NLQC, which mimics the approach used by complexity theorists: we study the relative hardness of different NLQC tasks by identifying resource efficient reductions between them. Most significantly, we prove that [MATH]-measure and [MATH]-route, the two best studied NLQC tasks, are in fact equivalent under [MATH] overhead reductions. This result simplifies many existing proofs in the literature and extends several new properties to [MATH]-measure. For instance, we obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on [MATH]-measure for all functions, and efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class [MATH]. Beyond this, we study a number of other examples of NLQC tasks and their relationships.

.
tldr: This paper develops a complexity-theoretic framework for non-local quantum computation, showing equivalence between two key tasks and providing efficient protocols for functions in certain complexity classes.
motivation: Characterizing the entanglement cost of non-local quantum computation is known to be hard; the authors aim to circumvent this by studying relative hardness via reductions, similar to classical complexity theory.
method: The authors define resource-efficient reductions between NLQC tasks and prove that the two best-studied tasks, f-measure and f-route, are equivalent under polynomial overhead reductions.
result: They obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on f-measure for all functions and efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class P, and extend several properties from f-route to f-measure.
conclusion: The reduction approach simplifies existing proofs and provides new insights into the resource requirements of NLQC, linking it to complexity theory.

title: On The Addressability Problem On Css Codes
authors: Jérôme Guyot And Samuel Jaques
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2145 (2026).

Recent discoveries in asymptotically good quantum codes have intensified research on their application in quantum computation and fault-tolerant operations. This study focuses on the addressability problem within CSS codes: we ask what circuits might implement logical gates on strict subsets of logical qubits. With some notion of fault-tolerance, we prove several impossibility results: for CSS codes with non-zero rate, one cannot address a logical [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], or [MATH] to any non-empty strict subset of logical qubits using a circuit made only from 1-local Clifford gates. Furthermore, we show that one cannot permute the logical qubits in a code purely by permuting the physical qubits, if the rate of the code is (asymptotically) greater than 1/3 and the distance is at least 3. We can show a similar no-go result for [MATH]s and [MATH]s between two such high-rate codes, albeit under a more restrictive assumption on the circuit, which we call "global" (though recent addressable CCZ gates use global circuits). This work pioneers the study of distance-preserving addressability in quantum codes, mainly by considering automorphisms of the code. This perspective offers new insights and potential directions for future research. We argue that studying this trade off between addressability and efficiency of the codes is essential to understand better how to do efficient quantum computation.

.
tldr: This paper proves impossibility results for addressing logical qubits in high-rate CSS codes using local Clifford circuits, and shows that permuting logical qubits via physical permutations is limited by code rate.
motivation: Understanding how to implement logical gates on subsets of logical qubits is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially with asymptotically good codes.
method: The authors use automorphism theory of CSS codes and combinatorial arguments to derive no-go theorems for addressability under local Clifford circuits and physical permutations.
result: For CSS codes with non-zero rate, one cannot address logical X, Z, H, or S gates to a strict subset of logical qubits using 1-local Clifford circuits. Also, permuting logical qubits via physical permutations is impossible if the rate > 1/3 and distance ≥ 3.
conclusion: There is a fundamental trade-off between addressability and code efficiency, which must be considered for practical quantum computation.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: A theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering where time-dependent control over a quantum system manipulates its environment, with applications to open quantum systems.
motivation: Standard quantum reservoir engineering uses a structured environment as an entropy sink, but active control can unlock new functionalities by allowing the system to act as an entropy sink for the environment.
method: The authors develop a framework capturing the dynamical interplay between system and environment, including finite-size effects and correlations, and illustrate with examples of a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: Qualitative agreement with previous experimental results is found, demonstrating that active control can manipulate the environment via repeated initialization of the quantum system.
conclusion: Active reservoir engineering provides a versatile tool for open quantum systems, enabling new control over dissipative processes.

title: A Non-Commutative Voronovskaya Theorem For Quantum Neural Network Operators
authors: Delvonei Alves de Andrade R\^omulo Damasclin Chaves Dos Santos
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a complete asymptotic expansion for quantum neural network operators when they approximate arbitrary quantum channels. This is the non-commutative analogue of the classical Voronovskaya theorem. The expansion reveals that the approximation error splits into three fundamentally different parts: integer powers of \(1/n\) involving ordinary Fr\'echet derivatives; fractional powers governed by Marchaud fractional derivatives, which capture the H\"older smoothness of the channel; and purely quantum commutator terms that have no classical counterpart. The remainder is bounded sharply by an explicit constant: \[ (\Phi,\bullet)}_\diamond \le C_{m,\gamma,d} \|\Phi\|_{\cC^{m,\gamma}} \, n^{-(m+\gamma)} (\log n)^{3m/2}. \] We present a numerical test for a classical analogue that confirms the predicted convergence rate and the logarithmic correction, directly validating the asymptotic theory. Based on this expansion, we obtain three major advances: a quantum central limit theorem for the fluctuations of quantum neural network operators, a method to construct optimal interpolation geodesics between quantum channels via Kubo-Ando means, and a systematic understanding of how fractional smoothness limits the acceleration of quantum neural network approximations. The numerical test further demonstrates that the theoretical rates are sharp and that logarithmic enhancements are unavoidable. Altogether, our work builds a rigorous bridge between classical approximation theory, fractional calculus, and quantum machine learning, offering both theoretical insight and practical tools for designing and analyzing quantum neural networks in finite dimensions.
tldr: Proves a non-commutative Voronovskaya theorem for quantum neural network operators, providing a complete asymptotic expansion of approximation error.
motivation: To understand the approximation properties of quantum neural networks and bridge classical approximation theory with quantum machine learning.
method: Uses Fréchet derivatives, Marchaud fractional derivatives, and commutator terms to derive an asymptotic expansion, with a numerical test for a classical analogue.
result: The error splits into integer powers, fractional powers, and quantum commutator terms; a sharp remainder bound is given, and a quantum central limit theorem is obtained.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous theoretical foundations for quantum neural network approximation, with implications for designing and analyzing quantum machine learning models.

title: Hybrid Nanophotonic Trap For Cold Atoms Using Surface Forces And A Blue-detuned Evanescent Field
authors: Riccardo Pennetta
Antoine Glicenstein
Lucas Pache

abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 09 July 2026;
tldr: A hybrid nanophotonic trap for cold atoms using surface forces and blue-detuned evanescent fields achieves efficient loading and enhanced storage and coherence times.
motivation: To improve the performance of atom-based quantum technologies by developing a robust and efficient trap for cold atoms near nanophotonic structures.
method: The trap combines attractive surface forces (Casimir-Polder) with repulsive blue-detuned evanescent fields to create a stable trapping potential for caesium atoms near a nanophotonic waveguide.
result: The hybrid trap demonstrates efficient loading, long storage times, and long coherence times, outperforming previous approaches.
conclusion: This hybrid trapping scheme is promising for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems, enabling strong atom-light interactions with low loss.

title: Witnessing Entanglement In Mixed-particle Quantum Systems
authors: Irma Avdic And David A. Mazziotti
abstract:
Author(s): Irma Avdic and David A. Mazziotti

We introduce an entanglement witness that identifies off-diagonal long-range order (ODLRO)—a distinctive form of entanglement—in systems containing both fermionic and bosonic particles. By analyzing the particle-hole reduced density matrices of each subsystem, the approach detects ODLRO independentl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051104] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces an entanglement witness for mixed-particle systems detecting off-diagonal long-range order via particle-hole reduced density matrices.
motivation: Extending entanglement detection to systems with both fermions and bosons is important for understanding quantum correlations in mixed-particle settings.
method: Analyzes particle-hole reduced density matrices of each subsystem to detect ODLRO independently of particle statistics.
result: The witness successfully identifies ODLRO in mixed-particle quantum systems.

title: Smallest Quantum Codes For Amplitude-damping Noise
authors: Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, And Prabha Mandayam
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, and Prabha Mandayam

This work presents a three-qubit quantum error correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends it to a family of codes that correct amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order in the damping strength. These codes are placed within a larger algebraic framework of probabilistic quantum error correction, which allows for postselected recovery and also leads to a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound for amplitude-damping noise.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032004] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a three-qubit quantum error-correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends to a family of codes for higher-order damping.
motivation: Amplitude-damping noise is a common decoherence mechanism in quantum systems, and existing quantum error-correcting codes are not optimized for this specific noise model. The authors aim to design minimal codes tailored to amplitude-damping noise.
method: The authors construct a three-qubit code that corrects single-qubit amplitude-damping errors using a noise-adapted approach, and generalize it to a family of codes for any fixed order of damping. They also develop a probabilistic quantum error correction framework with postselected recovery and derive a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound.
result: The three-qubit code corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors, and the family of codes corrects amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order. The noise-adapted Hamming bound provides a fundamental limit on code size for such noise.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that small, noise-adapted quantum codes can efficiently correct amplitude-damping errors, offering practical advantages for quantum memory and communication in realistic noisy environments.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions

abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, surpassing classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing beyond classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including scaling analysis and Fisher information.
result: It demonstrates how critical quantum systems can achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity and provides practical guidelines for experimental implementation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for next-generation metrology, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Multi-product Zeno Effect Achieving Higher Order Convergence Rates
authors: Tim Möbus
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2148 (2026).

The quantum Zeno effect is a fundamental mechanism for implementing the effective dynamics of projected Hamiltonian and Lindbladian systems. It approximates the target projected evolution by interleaving Hamiltonian or Lindblad dynamics with quantum operations associated with the desired subspace. In contrast to the related Trotter product formula, the best-known convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect is typically limited to order [MATH]. In this work, we improve this convergence rate by employing a multi-product formula, thereby achieving arbitrarily high-order convergence of the form [MATH]. This yields an improved approximation scheme for Zeno-like expectation values via an efficient post-processing method. The approach combines a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation. We illustrate the method with the bosonic cat code and also consider the broader class of systems governed by the Bang-Bang decoupling method.

.
tldr: This paper improves the convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect to arbitrarily high order using a multi-product formula, with applications to projected Hamiltonian and Lindbladian dynamics.
motivation: The quantum Zeno effect typically has a convergence rate limited to first order; achieving higher-order convergence would enable more accurate approximations of projected dynamics.
method: The authors combine a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation to construct a multi-product formula that yields higher-order convergence.
result: They demonstrate arbitrarily high-order convergence of the form O(Δt^k) for the quantum Zeno effect, and illustrate the method with the bosonic cat code and Bang-Bang decoupling.
conclusion: The multi-product Zeno effect provides a systematic way to improve approximation accuracy for Zeno-like expectation values, with potential applications in quantum control and simulation.

title: Comment On Temperature Change Can Solve The Deutsch-Jozsa Problem: An Exploration Of Thermodynamic Query Complexity
authors: Ridha Horchani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the readout analysis in Phys. Rev. A 113, 012420 (2026) does not establish the claimed resource accounting of one thermal query followed by many statistically useful probe samples. A CNOT fanout of a diagonal post-query probe broadcasts its one-qubit marginal but produces perfectly correlated registers rather than independent copies. Consequently, neither the trace distance nor the relative entropy between the balanced and constant hypotheses increases, and repeated measurements of the ancillas provide only one Bernoulli observation. Independent samples instead require repeated preparation and heat exchange, which are repeated queries under the definition adopted in the original paper. We also show that the sample lower bound stated there does not follow from Pinsker's inequality: the inequality gives the opposite ordering for the reciprocal relative entropy. The thermal-kickback mechanism may still encode the decision in the probe temperature, but the one-query readout claim and the quoted necessity of approximately 116 samples require correction.
tldr: This comment refutes a claimed one-query thermodynamic solution to the Deutsch-Jozsa problem, showing that the original paper's resource accounting and sample lower bound are incorrect.
motivation: The original paper claimed that a single thermal query could solve the Deutsch-Jozsa problem by measuring probe temperature, which would have significant implications for query complexity. This comment corrects the analysis.
method: The author analyzes the original protocol's readout scheme, showing that a CNOT fanout produces correlated registers, not independent copies, and that Pinsker's inequality does not support the claimed sample lower bound.
result: The comment demonstrates that the trace distance and relative entropy between hypotheses do not increase with repeated measurements, and that independent samples require repeated queries, not just one.
conclusion: The claimed one-query readout and the necessity of approximately 116 samples are incorrect; the thermal-kickback mechanism may still work but requires correction of the resource accounting.

title: Comment On Statistical Mechanics From Quantum Envariance And Exchange Symmetry
authors: Ridha Horchani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ojha, Sardana, and Ghosh [Phys. Rev. A 113, 042221 (2026)] propose that tracing environmental records of particle permutations produces an entropy kB ln N!, thereby explaining the Gibbs factor, and use the same construction to multiply the Saha equilibrium relation by 1/(Ne!Np!). We show that these conclusions do not follow. The reduced density matrix printed in their Eq. (32) is not a partial trace, and even under the natural corrected interpretation the entropy equals kB ln N! only when the system branch states are mutually orthogonal. That condition is not generally satisfied and, when imposed on labeled permutation branches, does not by itself restrict the particle state to one bosonic or fermionic symmetry sector. A two-particle calculation makes the contradiction explicit. Their Gibbs-paradox calculation also starts from a distinguishable-particle entropy while calling it the Sackur-Tetrode entropy. In the Saha section, the state in Eq. (52), as written, factorizes and has zero system-environment entanglement. The proposed factorial does not approach unity in the claimed dilute-gas limit, does not yield a finite nonzero intensive thermodynamic limit, and counts indistinguishability twice. We give the corrected canonical and fugacity-based formulations and identify which standard results of the paper remain unaffected.
tldr: This comment identifies errors in a paper claiming to derive the Gibbs factor and Saha equilibrium from quantum envariance and exchange symmetry, showing the entropy argument fails unless branch states are orthogonal and the Saha factor double-counts indistinguishability.
motivation: The original paper attempted to explain the Gibbs paradox and Saha equilibrium using quantum envariance, but the comment shows the derivations are flawed, which is important for correct statistical mechanics foundations.
method: The comment analyzes the original paper's density matrix and partial trace operations, constructs a two-particle counterexample, and examines the thermodynamic limit of the proposed factorial factor.
result: The reduced density matrix in the original paper is not a proper partial trace; the entropy equals kB ln N! only under orthogonal branch states, which is not generally satisfied; the Saha factor does not approach unity in the dilute-gas limit and double-counts indistinguishability.
conclusion: The claimed derivations of the Gibbs factor and Saha equilibrium from quantum envariance are incorrect, and the corrected formulations are provided.

The paper also points out that OSG's Gibbs-paradox calculation mistakenly uses a distinguishable-particle entropy while calling it the Sackur-Tetrode entropy. In the Saha section, OSG's state factorizes with zero system-environment entanglement, and their proposed factorial does not approach unity in the dilute-gas limit, fails to yield a finite intensive thermodynamic limit, and double-counts indistinguishability. title: Quantum-classical Neurons Upgraded With Optical Spin Qubits For Advanced Computing And Networking Architectures
authors: Osama M. Nayfeh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware neurons incorporating built-in memory components are critical technologies for implementing large scale neural networks that exhibit adaptive-itinerant behavior and produce biological-inspired spiking patterns that match neuroscience known operations (1). Moreover, neurons capable of full quantum information processing through their qubit states and quantum trajectory provides capability for hybrid quantum-classical operations through the level of coherence/entanglement and non-Markovianity (2,3). These attributes further contribute to solving complex quantum mechanical problems by providing a rich and diverse group for expressing quantum neural states. Upgrading these hardware neurons now with optical spin qubits excitable with pulsed laser excitation in the near infrared and designed from negatively charged silicon vacancies in semiconductor silicon carbide (4) and Neodymium rare earth ions in the superconducting Niobium/Niobium oxide film (5) that form the memory provides access to the unique spin Hamiltonian that considers electronic and nuclear interactions. In this manuscript, we experimentally measure opto-electronic quantum-classical neurons integrated with a optical spin qubit and examine how tailored neuronal spiking sequences drive the photoluminescence oscillations and modulate the quantum spin transitions. We derive a quantum model for the system that considers the interaction between the neuron and optical qubit spin and perform calculations to project how quantum computing operations are expandable across the state space in the quantum-classical neuron and spin qubit system. For example, the resulting impact on the neuron quantum states where the strength is adjustable due to dynamical memory changes. These results are critical for realizing hardware neurons with quantum optical capabilities and inspired by the existence in biology of biophotons.

motivation: To create hardware neurons with built-in memory and quantum capabilities that can emulate biological spiking patterns and perform quantum information processing.
method: The authors fabricate opto-electronic quantum-classical neurons integrated with optical spin qubits, use pulsed laser excitation to drive photoluminescence, and derive a quantum model for the neuron-qubit interaction.
result: They show that tailored neuronal spiking sequences modulate quantum spin transitions and photoluminescence oscillations, and that quantum operations can be expanded across the combined state space.
conclusion: These results are critical for realizing hardware neurons with quantum optical capabilities, inspired by biophotons in biology.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Scalable Quantum Blockchain With Exponentially Superior Quantum Communication Complexity
authors: Feng Xie, Ming-Yang Li, Yongqiang Du, Chen-Xun Weng, Mingxuan Zhang, Xin Hua, Xiang Guan, Xin An, Jingzhe He, Xin Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, Xi Xiao, Hua-Lei Yin, Kejin Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To secure modern distributed digital infrastructures, quantum blockchains exploit quantum resources to achieve information-theoretic security and surpass the classical one-third fault-tolerance bound. However, existing high-fault-tolerant protocols face a fundamental scalability challenge: the blockchain trilemma imposes either exponential communication complexity or experimentally demanding multipartite entanglement. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable quantum blockchain protocol based on weak coherent states that achieves an exponential reduction in quantum communication complexity. The protocol employs a circular quantum Byzantine agreement mechanism that preserves information-theoretic security while avoiding multipartite entanglement. We implement this protocol on a photonic integrated circuit platform, realizing a six-node network over commercially available telecommunication infrastructure. Compared with previous schemes, the protocol requires less than 4% of the quantum communication resources. Leveraging this advantage, we further demonstrate a quantum-secured token exchange application achieving a throughput of 805.3 transactions per second with zero failures. These results establish a practical pathway toward scalable quantum blockchain.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a scalable quantum blockchain protocol using weak coherent states that achieves exponential reduction in quantum communication complexity.
motivation: Existing quantum blockchain protocols face scalability issues due to exponential communication complexity or reliance on experimentally demanding multipartite entanglement. This work aims to overcome these challenges.
method: The protocol employs a circular quantum Byzantine agreement mechanism using weak coherent states, avoiding multipartite entanglement. It is implemented on a photonic integrated circuit platform over telecom infrastructure.
result: A six-node network is demonstrated, requiring less than 4% of the quantum communication resources of previous schemes, and a quantum-secured token exchange achieves 805.3 transactions per second with zero failures.
conclusion: This work establishes a practical pathway toward scalable quantum blockchain, demonstrating exponential improvement in communication complexity and high throughput.

title: From Stable Periodic Orbits To Many-body Chaos: Doubly Tunable Prethermalization Via Engineering Of An Emergent Band Structure
authors: Jianan Wang, Yang Hou, Andrea Pizzi, Johannes Knolle, Roderich Moessner, Hongzheng Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We uncover a family of many-body periodic orbits in a periodically driven (Floquet) spin system away from the high-frequency limit. While linear stability analysis predicts that perturbed many-body trajectories remain close to stable periodic orbits, thermodynamic principles dictate that Floquet heating will ultimately set in. Our work aims to resolve the tension between these two expectations. In particular, we show that perturbations away from the stable periodic orbits feature a description akin to a quasiparticle band structure. A long-lived prethermal regime appears when modes around the gapless point are slowly populated. The dispersion determines the prethermal lifetime, and we show how band engineering leads to a "doubly tunable" parametric dependence of the prethermal lifetime [MATH], with [MATH] the width in momentum space of the quasiparticle distribution and [MATH] the exponent of the dispersion around the gapless point. Our results not only establish a powerful route toward stabilizing non-equilibrium phases of matter in driven many-body systems but also establish a conceptual bridge between periodic orbits in 'low-dimensional' nonlinear systems and many-body chaos.
tldr: This paper studies prethermalization in a driven spin system by engineering an emergent band structure, linking stable periodic orbits to many-body chaos.
motivation: To resolve the tension between linear stability of periodic orbits and inevitable Floquet heating in many-body systems.
method: They analyze perturbations around stable periodic orbits in a Floquet spin system, mapping them to a quasiparticle band structure and deriving the prethermal lifetime from the dispersion.
result: The prethermal lifetime depends on the momentum width of the quasiparticle distribution and the dispersion exponent, enabling doubly tunable control.
conclusion: Band engineering provides a powerful route to stabilize non-equilibrium phases and bridges low-dimensional periodic orbits with many-body chaos.

title: Strain-Induced Detuning Of A Dressed Nitrogen-Vacancy Qubit: Effective Two-Level Theory And Its Validity
authors: Jihyeon Jeon, Donghun Lee, Seok-Kyun Son, Nojoon Myoung
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond can be operated as a microwave-dressed qubit. In the ideal two-level limit, its transition frequency is first-order insensitive to static magnetic fields, providing robustness against magnetic detuning noise. In practical diamond devices, however, residual transverse crystal strain mixes the [MATH] spin sublevels and modifies the dressed qubit. In this study, we derive an analytical effective two-level model of a strained dressed NV qubit by perturbatively eliminating the far-detuned spectator state from the full three-level dressed Hamiltonian. We obtain closed-form expressions for the dressed-state splitting, the spin-locking mixing angle, and the longitudinal magnetic-field coupling. We show that transverse strain shifts the dressed-state resonance and tilts the spin-locking axis. These two effects restore a finite DC-field response and thereby quantify the loss of magnetic robustness. We demonstrate these features in simulated pulsed electron spin resonance spectra that incorporate rate-equation-based optical readout. We further derive exact validity criteria from the eigenvalues and spectator weights of the full three-level Hamiltonian. For practical use, we reduce these criteria to two controlled guidelines: the spectator-like branch must remain above the nominal upper dressed state, and its branch-specific admixture must remain small. A validity diagram over the axial-field--transverse-strain plane summarizes these approximate conditions and provides practical guidelines for designing dressed-NV sensing experiments.
tldr: This paper develops an effective two-level model for a strained dressed NV qubit, quantifying the loss of magnetic robustness due to transverse strain.
motivation: Dressed NV qubits are promising for quantum sensing due to magnetic insensitivity, but residual strain in diamond devices degrades performance. A practical model is needed to understand and mitigate this effect.
method: The authors derive an analytical effective two-level Hamiltonian by perturbatively eliminating the far-detuned spectator state from the full three-level dressed system, obtaining closed-form expressions for dressed-state splitting, mixing angle, and magnetic field coupling.
result: Transverse strain shifts the dressed-state resonance and tilts the spin-locking axis, restoring a finite DC-field response. Validity criteria are derived and summarized in a diagram over axial-field–transverse-strain plane.
conclusion: The effective model provides practical guidelines for designing robust dressed-NV sensors, highlighting the trade-off between strain and magnetic field robustness.

authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:

Because of its parabolic character, the diffusion equation exhibits instantaneous spatial spreading and becomes unstable when Lorentz boosted. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022302] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the diffusion equation can be made compatible with special relativity by reformulating it as a relativistic field theory.
motivation: The diffusion equation is parabolic and violates causality when Lorentz boosted, which has been seen as a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity. The author aims to resolve this paradox.
method: The author reinterprets the diffusion equation as a relativistic field equation by introducing a suitable Lagrangian and applying the principle of least action, leading to a hyperbolic system that respects causality.
result: The resulting relativistic diffusion equation is causal and Lorentz covariant, eliminating instantaneous spreading and instability under boosts.
conclusion: Diffusion processes can be described consistently within special relativity, bridging a gap between non-equilibrium thermodynamics and relativistic physics.

Due to its localized nature and controllability, the negatively charged boron vacancy centers ([MATH]) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are a promising spin platform for accessing its neighboring nuclei with potential for performing quantum computational tasks. However, the me…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033047] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to arbitrarily manipulate nuclear spins in hexagonal boron nitride using boron vacancy centers, enabling quantum computational tasks.
motivation: Nuclear spins in hBN are promising for quantum computing but lack full control; the authors aim to achieve arbitrary single-qubit gates on these spins.
method: They design a protocol using the negatively charged boron vacancy center as a mediator, applying microwave and radiofrequency pulses to control the nuclear spin via hyperfine interaction.
result: The scheme allows universal control of nuclear spins with high fidelity, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work establishes hBN as a viable platform for quantum information processing with nuclear spins.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and engineered interactions to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization to prove composable security.
result: They achieve a secret key rate of over 1 Mbps over 50 km of fiber, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD implementations.
conclusion: The results show that discrete-modulated CV-QKD can be both high-rate and provably secure, bringing practical quantum networks closer to deployment.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent manipulation.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a key tool for using circular Rydberg atoms in quantum computing and networking applications.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum computing, but two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around a tweezer array of cesium atoms, suppressing blackbody radiation and measuring Rydberg lifetimes at various temperatures.
result: At cryogenic temperatures, Rydberg lifetimes are extended by over an order of magnitude compared to room temperature, directly reducing the dominant relaxation error in two-qubit gates.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to significantly improve neutral-atom quantum computer fidelities, enabling fault-tolerant quantum computing with Rydberg arrays.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
