title: Counting Connected And Disconnected Ways To Assemble A Jigsaw Puzzle
authors: Prarthana Agrawal, Abdurrahman Hadi Erturk, Ard A. Louis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A jigsaw puzzle may be assembled in many different ways. Some assembly sequences remain connected throughout, while others temporarily build separate parts of the puzzle before joining them together. By representing the puzzle as a graph, these assembly sequences become vertex orderings that can be counted using recent results from graph theory. We apply this framework to enumerate three natural assembly strategies: connected assembly, assembly beginning from several disconnected pieces, and assembly in which new disconnected sections may be started during the process. The resulting counts reveal that, even for modest puzzle sizes, connectivity-preserving assembly sequences are greatly outnumbered by those that pass through disconnected intermediate stages.
tldr: This paper uses graph theory to count assembly sequences of jigsaw puzzles, comparing connected and disconnected strategies.
motivation: Understanding the combinatorial complexity of assembly processes, which may have implications for self-assembly or manufacturing.
method: Representing the puzzle as a graph and applying graph-theoretic counting of vertex orderings for three assembly strategies.
result: For modest puzzle sizes, connected assembly sequences are vastly outnumbered by those that pass through disconnected intermediate stages.
conclusion: Disconnected assembly strategies are combinatorially dominant, suggesting that natural or engineered assembly processes may often involve temporary disconnected components.

title: Analytical Evaluation Of Ramanujan Series For $1/\pi$ Via Degree-2, Degree-3, Degree-7 And Degree-19 Modular Equations
authors: Pablo Fern\'andez Refolio
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide an explicit analytical evaluation of Ramanujan-type series for [MATH]. Focusing on the singular moduli [MATH],[MATH],[MATH],[MATH] and [MATH]. We demonstrate that the underlying elliptic identities can be established through lower-degree modular equations; specifically, we resolve the cases [MATH] utilizing the modular equation of degree 2, the case [MATH] via a combination of degree-2 and degree-3 modular equations, the case [MATH] via a combination of degree-2 and degree-7 modular equations and the case [MATH] via a combination of degree-2 and degree-19 modular equations. In the first part of this work, we confine our attention to hypergeometric theory and elliptic integrals. Subsequently, in the second part, we extend our framework to incorporate the theory of elliptic functions, which allows us to address the higher-complexity modular identities.

motivation: To provide explicit analytical evaluations of Ramanujan-type series for 1/π by establishing underlying elliptic identities through lower-degree modular equations.
method: The authors use hypergeometric theory and elliptic integrals in the first part, and extend to elliptic functions in the second part to handle higher-complexity modular identities.
result: They successfully evaluate series for singular moduli using degree-2, degree-3, degree-7, and degree-19 modular equations.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that Ramanujan-type series can be evaluated analytically using lower-degree modular equations, contributing to the theory of elliptic functions and modular forms.

title: A Ramanujan Pell Elliptic K3 Surface And Primitive Five-Cube Near Misses
authors: K. Srinivasa Raghava
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a trace-16 Ramanujan--Pell family of primitive positive five-cube near misses \[ a_n^3+b_n^3+c_n^3+d_n^3+e_n^3=t_n^3+(-1)^{n+1}, \] obtained from a six-cube identity of quadratic forms and the negative Pell orbit generated by \(8+\). The six coefficient sequences have rational recurrence generating functions with common reciprocal denominator \[ R(q)=1-257q-257q^2+q^3=(1+q)(1-258q+q^2). \] The quadratic identity is derived from a conic source, explaining the constants, while the Pell mechanism accounts for both the alternating error term and the denominator. The same construction yields the Mordell curve \[ E_K:\ y^2=x^3-432K(u)^2,\qquad K(u)=(1-13u+26u^2)^3+(6+182u^2)^3. \] We prove that its minimal smooth projective model is an elliptic K3 surface with geometric fibre configuration \(6IV\); over \(\mathbb Q\), the singular-fibre divisor is supported at one degree-two and one degree-four closed point. The section induced by the displayed decomposition of \(K\) has canonical height \(4/3\). The torsion groups over \(\mathbb Q(u)\), \(\mathbb Q()(u)\), and \((u)\) are respectively \(0\), \(\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z\), and \(\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z\). Over \(\mathbb Q()(u)\), the complex multiplication orbit of the section gives an Eisenstein Mordell--Weil sublattice and a visible generated rank-16 sublattice of the geometric Neron--Severi group of discriminant \(-108\); no fullness or primitivity is claimed. We identify the remaining free Mordell--Weil problem with an explicit equivariant Hom module, exhibit an anti-symplectic reciprocal involution, and show that \(w^3=K(u)\) has a Fermat-cubic quotient. No modularity assertion is made for the recurrence functions.
tldr: This paper constructs a Ramanujan-Pell family of five-cube near misses and studies an associated elliptic K3 surface, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper is motivated by number theory and algebraic geometry, specifically the construction of Diophantine equations and elliptic surfaces.
method: The authors use quadratic forms, Pell equations, and rational recurrences to derive a family of five-cube near misses, then analyze the associated Mordell curve and its K3 surface model.
result: They obtain a trace-16 Ramanujan-Pell family with alternating error term, and prove that the minimal smooth projective model is an elliptic K3 surface with specific fibre configuration and torsion groups.
conclusion: The work contributes to the study of Diophantine equations and elliptic surfaces, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Boolean Walsh Eta Units And Eisenstein Bases For Squarefree Levels
authors: K. Srinivasa Raghava
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be squarefree and let [MATH] be its Boolean divisor cube. To each Boolean character [MATH] we attach the eta-quotient \[ R_T^{(M)}(\tau)=\prod_{d\mid M}\eta(d\tau)^{\chi_T(d)}, \qquad \chi_T(d)=(-1)^{|T\cap\supp(d)|}. \] At squarefree level, the finite Fourier transform on the divisor cube simultaneously diagonalizes the squarefree Ligozat cusp-order matrix, Fricke complementation, Atkin--Lehner action on cusp labels, and the constant-term map for logarithmic Eisenstein series. In particular, for [MATH], \[ \ord_{1/c}R_T^{(M)} =}{24}\chi_T(c), \qquad \Lambda_T^{(M)}= \prod_{p\in T}(p-1) \prod_{}(p+1), \] and the forms [MATH] form a Walsh basis of the Eisenstein subspace of [MATH]. The structural theorem also determines explicit Fricke constants, Atkin--Lehner eigenvalues, good-prime Hecke eigenvalues, local [MATH] triangular blocks, a simultaneous bad-prime eigenbasis, and the indices of two explicit principal cuspidal divisor sublattices inside the formal degree-zero cusp-divisor lattice. As an application we specialize to the Heegner prime product \[ N=2\cdot3\cdot7\cdot11\cdot19\cdot43\cdot67\cdot163. \] The first Boolean boundary gives the eta-normalized Heegner-coloured partition product, while the top Walsh character gives the M\"obius eta-unit identity \[ D\log R_{\mathcal P}^{(N)}(\tau)=40415760- \sum_{n\ge1}\sigma_1(n^\perp)q^n. \] The same application gives algebraic modular-unit relations for the reciprocal partition product and exact Fricke-fixed logarithmic derivative identities for [MATH], interpreted through the modular completion of [MATH] and through accelerated paired products.
tldr: This paper studies Boolean Walsh eta units and Eisenstein bases for squarefree levels in number theory, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to develop a structural theory for eta-quotients and Eisenstein series at squarefree levels using Boolean Fourier analysis on divisor cubes.
method: It defines eta-quotients indexed by Boolean characters on the divisor cube, computes their orders and Fourier transforms, and derives explicit formulas for Fricke constants, Atkin-Lehner eigenvalues, and Hecke eigenvalues.
result: The forms form a Walsh basis of the Eisenstein subspace, and explicit identities are given for a specific Heegner prime product, including a Möbius eta-unit identity.
conclusion: The work provides a complete algebraic description of the Eisenstein subspace at squarefree levels, with applications to modular units and partition products.

title: Generalized q-Morgan Voyce Polynomials
authors: Yuksel Soykan Bahad{\i}r Y{\i}lmaz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study introduces and investigates generalized q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials and their specific cases, including the first and second kinds of q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials, q-Horadam-Morgan-Voyce polynomials, and Fibonacci-type q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials. The generalized q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials are defined by the recurrence relation featuring the specific q-power q^{n-2} and a negative sign, formulated as M_{n}(x,q) = (x+1+q)M_{n-1}(x,q) - q^{n-2}M_{n-2}(x,q) for n >= 2. The generating functions and explicit expressions for these polynomials are established by utilizing the Fibonacci operator and the binomial theorem. Furthermore, the study extends these polynomials to negative indices and derives the corresponding explicit formulas. Summation formulas and determinantal presentations of the generalized polynomials and their special cases are also comprehensively provided. Finally, the q-Cassini's formula for the generalized q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials is established through the definition of specific square matrices and their subsequent recurrence relations.
tldr: This paper introduces and studies generalized q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials, a family of q-analog polynomials defined by a recurrence relation, and derives their generating functions, explicit expressions, and combinatorial properties.
motivation: The study aims to extend the theory of Morgan-Voyce polynomials to a q-analog setting, exploring their properties and connections to other polynomial families.
method: The authors define the polynomials via a recurrence relation involving q-powers, use the Fibonacci operator and binomial theorem to derive generating functions and explicit formulas, and employ matrix methods to obtain determinantal presentations and q-Cassini's formula.
result: The paper provides generating functions, explicit expressions, summation formulas, determinantal presentations, and q-Cassini's identity for the generalized q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials and their special cases.
conclusion: The work contributes to the combinatorial theory of q-polynomials but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Crack Growth Forecasting Via Conditional Denoising Diffusion Models For Phase-Field Fracture
authors: S. M. Mallikarjunaiah Jahnavi Krishna Koda
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The accurate prediction of brittle crack initiation, propagation, and complex topological evolution remains computationally prohibitive when utilizing traditional high-fidelity phase-field finite element methods. To overcome these computational bottlenecks, a physics-informed conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) is proposed for the full-field spatiotemporal forecasting of fracture evolution across diverse loading regimes and energy decomposition methods. The generative architecture is conditioned on rolling historical damage states and explicitly derived kinematic proxies -- phase-field velocity and gradient magnitude -- ensuring temporal coherence without non-physical artifacts. The principal contribution is spatially-localized uncertainty quantification without modification to the trained model. Ensemble variance concentrates at crack branching junctions ([MATH] at Y-junction bifurcations; zero high-uncertainty pixels in four deterministic propagation cases), while the high-[MATH] tail identifies high-error predictions with 90\% precision -- an 18-fold improvement over random selection. One-step crack tip localization achieves sub-pixel accuracy (0.12 px mean error) across both held-out validation subsets (shear-star and tension-spect), confirming cross-regime generalization. In closed-loop autoregressive rollout over 50 steps, the DDPM maintains Dice = 0.929 [MATH] 0.010 while a deterministic U-Net collapses to Dice = 0.423 under error accumulation, a 2.2[MATH] gap that establishes the value of stochastic re-sampling for long-horizon stability. Per-step inference requires approximately 3.6 s on an H100 GPU, approximately 28[MATH] faster than the FEM reference and 1{,}000[MATH] slower than a deterministic U-Net a cost that buys the stochastic diversity enabling uncertainty quantification.
tldr: This paper uses a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model for forecasting brittle crack propagation in phase-field fracture, with uncertainty quantification.
motivation: Traditional high-fidelity phase-field finite element methods are computationally prohibitive for predicting crack evolution; a faster surrogate model with uncertainty quantification is needed.
method: A physics-informed conditional DDPM is trained on historical damage states and kinematic proxies (phase-field velocity and gradient magnitude) to forecast fracture fields; ensemble variance provides uncertainty estimates.
result: The DDPM achieves sub-pixel crack tip localization (0.12 px error), maintains Dice=0.929 over 50 autoregressive steps (vs. 0.423 for U-Net), and identifies high-error predictions with 90% precision.
conclusion: Stochastic generative models offer long-horizon stability and built-in uncertainty quantification for fracture forecasting, outperforming deterministic baselines.

title: The Maximal Volume Of Projections Of The Cross-polytope
authors: Grigory Ivanov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the conjectured sharp upper bound for the volume of an arbitrary lower-dimensional orthogonal projection of the regular cross-polytope. More generally, for every spanning family [MATH] we prove \[ \nolimits_{k} \{\pm v_1, \dots, \pm v_n\} \le {k!} ^n v_i\otimes v_i\right)}. \] After the natural normalization, equality holds precisely when the non-zero vectors form an orthonormal basis. We triangulate the boundary of the absolute convex hull, compare the determinant of every radial simplex with the Gaussian solid angle of its positive cone, and then use that the radial cones form a complete fan. As a consequence, the volume of the projection of [MATH] onto any [MATH]-dimensional subspace is at most [MATH], with equality only for coordinate subspaces.
tldr: This paper proves a sharp upper bound for the volume of orthogonal projections of the regular cross-polytope, a purely geometric result.
motivation: The paper addresses a conjecture in convex geometry about the maximal volume of projections of the cross-polytope, which is a fundamental object in geometry.
method: The proof uses triangulation of the boundary of the absolute convex hull, compares determinants of radial simplices with Gaussian solid angles, and leverages the fact that radial cones form a complete fan.
result: The authors prove the conjectured sharp upper bound for the volume of any lower-dimensional orthogonal projection of the regular cross-polytope, with equality only for coordinate subspaces.
conclusion: The result settles a geometric conjecture and provides a complete characterization of extremal projections.

title: Tangent-Space Multiscale Manifold Methods For Nonlinear Elliptic Problems
authors: Anna Persson Mats G. Larson
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a tangent-space multiscale manifold method for nonlinear heterogeneous elliptic problems. The method represents the fine-scale solution by a nonlinear reconstruction of a coarse state. The ideal reconstruction eliminates fine scales through a constrained variational problem, and the computable reconstruction approximates this map by localized nonlinear patch solves blended with a partition of unity. Because the approximation set is a nonlinear manifold, the coarse equation is posed with tangent multiscale test functions. We also formulate a network-interpolated variant in which only the restricted patch outputs used by the partition-of-unity blend, together with their tangent actions, are approximated by local learned maps. For heterogeneous monotone nonlinear diffusion, we record the structural monotonicity, differentiability, patch-map regularity, and conditional perturbation estimates that separate the geometric stability mechanism from localization, residual, and optional learning defects. A rigorous a priori theory for the decay of the localization defect, and the resulting convergence rates in the coarse mesh size, is deferred to a separate analysis; here these defects are controlled conditionally and their decay is demonstrated numerically.
tldr: This paper introduces a tangent-space multiscale manifold method for solving nonlinear heterogeneous elliptic problems, focusing on numerical methods for PDEs.
motivation: To efficiently solve nonlinear heterogeneous elliptic problems by representing fine-scale solutions through nonlinear reconstructions of coarse states.
method: The method uses a constrained variational problem for ideal reconstruction and approximates it with localized nonlinear patch solves blended via partition of unity, with a network-interpolated variant for efficiency.
result: The paper provides structural monotonicity, differentiability, and perturbation estimates, and demonstrates numerically the decay of localization defects.
conclusion: The method offers a rigorous framework for multiscale nonlinear problems, with convergence analysis deferred to future work.

title: Exact Solutions To A Class Of Constrained Optimal Control Problems Via Lossless Convexification For Digital Control
authors: Vaibhav Upadhyay, Siddhartha Ganguly, Debasish Chatterjee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article establishes a new numerically viable technique for solving a class of constrained, nonconvex, continuous-time optimal control problems (OCPs) for linear systems that commonly arise in aerial and aerospace applications. The lossless convexification technique is employed to translate the original nonconvex OCP with annular control magnitude constraints into a convex problem, and then by finitely parametrizing the control space with piecewise constant functions, an efficient numerical approach is established that guarantees exact solutions while ensuring the satisfaction of an uncountable family of constraints over a compact time interval. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated on a spacecraft landing problem involving three degrees of freedom (DoF), underscoring its potential for real-world aerospace guidance and control tasks.
tldr: This paper presents a lossless convexification technique for solving constrained optimal control problems in aerospace applications.
motivation: Aerospace guidance and control tasks often involve nonconvex optimal control problems with annular control constraints, which are challenging to solve exactly and efficiently.
method: The authors employ lossless convexification to transform the nonconvex OCP into a convex problem, then parametrize the control space with piecewise constant functions to obtain an exact numerical solution.
result: The approach guarantees exact solutions while satisfying an uncountable family of constraints over a compact time interval, demonstrated on a 3-DOF spacecraft landing problem.
conclusion: The proposed method provides an efficient and exact numerical technique for a class of constrained optimal control problems relevant to aerospace guidance and control.

title: Body-fitted Tracking Of 2d Open Curves With A Level Set Based Mesh Evolution Method
authors: Charles Dapogny
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article describes a novel numerical algorithm for tracking the motion of a collection of open curves in two space dimensions. The proposed strategy combines two complementary representations of these curves at each iteration of the evolution process: on the one hand, they are meshed explicitly, as a sub-collection of the entities of a mesh of the total computational domain. Concurrently, using a variant of the Level Set Method, they are captured implicitly as algebraic combinations of the negative, zero and positive subsets of two auxiliary scalar functions, defined on the whole ambient space. This coupling of representations allows to perform accurate geometric or mechanical computations on these curves, while leaving room for large evolution of their shape. After the description of its main numerical ingredients, several applications examples of this methodology are proposed, where it is used to simulate the motion of open physical discontinuities, such as a vortex sheet roll-up, and to optimize the shape of open-ended curves, e.g. with respect to their anisotropic length, with the aim to improve the trajectory of a laser acting on a powder bed in the context of additive manufacturing, or to reconstruct fracture sets.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical algorithm for tracking open curves in 2D using a hybrid explicit-implicit representation.
motivation: Tracking open curves with large deformations is challenging; existing methods either lack accuracy or cannot handle topological changes.
method: The method combines an explicit mesh representation of curves with a level set approach using two auxiliary scalar functions to capture curves implicitly.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on vortex sheet roll-up, shape optimization for additive manufacturing, and fracture set reconstruction.
conclusion: The hybrid representation enables accurate geometric computations while allowing large shape evolution, suitable for physical discontinuities and shape optimization.

title: Lqg Solution For Pomdp Without Estimating States: A Minimum Variance Approach
authors: Prabhat K. Mishra Ranjan Sarkar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the control of discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) systems subject to incomplete and corrupted measurements. Specifically, we focus on designing a Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) controller without relying on explicit state estimation. By leveraging minimum variance duality, our approach allows the current control input to be represented as a linear function of available measurements and previously applied inputs, successfully reducing the task to a tractable deterministic optimization problem. We provide theoretical justification for this framework and demonstrate its practical effectiveness through numerical experiments.
tldr: This paper proposes an LQG controller for LTI systems with incomplete measurements that avoids explicit state estimation using minimum variance duality.
motivation: To control systems with corrupted measurements without the need for state estimation, simplifying the controller design.
method: The control input is expressed as a linear function of past measurements and inputs, reducing the problem to a deterministic optimization via minimum variance duality.
result: Theoretical justification and numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a tractable alternative to standard LQG control with state estimation.

title: Broken-space Additive Schwarz Mass Inverse Approximations And (Block) Preconditioning
authors: Oliver A. Krzysik, Ben S. Southworth, Golo A. Wimmer
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-element mass matrix solves and approximate inverses arise often in explicit time integration as well as Schur-complement-based block preconditioning. A diagonal approximation of the mass matrix is cheap and widely used, but can be a poor approximation, particularly for high-order elements. This paper introduces a broken-space additive Schwarz (BRAS) mass inverse approximation, formed by applying exact element-local inverse mass matrices on the broken finite-element space and averaging the result back to the conforming space. The construction uses the same element matrices and local-to-global maps as standard mass assembly, has the same element-adjacency sparsity graph as the conforming mass matrix, and is symmetric positive definite for any conforming space, mesh geometry, and polynomial basis. We prove spectral bounds for the preconditioned mass matrix, and wide-ranging numerical experiments for \(H^1\), \(H()\), and \(H()\) finite elements on two- and three-dimensional simplicial meshes show that BRAS reduces spectral condition numbers, Krylov iterations, and solve times relative to diagonal preconditioning. For preconditioned conjugate gradient (CG), BRAS yields a 1.1--4.7[MATH] speedup over diagonal/Jacobi preconditioning across all cases tested over finite-element orders [MATH]. Further, theory and numerical experiments show that in the block-preconditioning case, BRAS can improve Schur-complement approximations and reduce outer solve times. On mixed Poisson and biharmonic systems, BRAS yields a 1.5--3[MATH] speedup in time-to-solution over a standard diagonal-based preconditioning approach.
tldr: This paper introduces a broken-space additive Schwarz mass inverse approximation for finite-element mass matrix solves, improving preconditioning efficiency.
motivation: Diagonal mass matrix approximations are cheap but poor for high-order elements; a better approximation is needed for explicit time integration and block preconditioning.
method: The BRAS method applies exact element-local inverse mass matrices on the broken finite-element space and averages back to the conforming space, using standard assembly data.
result: BRAS reduces spectral condition numbers, Krylov iterations, and solve times relative to diagonal preconditioning, achieving 1.1-4.7x speedup for CG and 1.5-3x for block preconditioning on mixed Poisson and biharmonic systems.
conclusion: BRAS is a symmetric positive definite preconditioner that outperforms diagonal preconditioning across various finite-element spaces and mesh geometries.

title: Stability And Bifurcations Of Planar Switched Linear And Homogeneous Systems
authors: Xinzhi Liu Ivan O. Shevchenko
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove new necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform asymptotic stability under arbitrary switching of two-dimensional switched homogeneous systems with a finite number of subsystems using a worst-case switching analysis. The novelty of our approach is in its explicit nature, which allows us to then study in detail the codimension-one bifurcations of stability of the origin in switched linear systems and further conclude new local and global stability results for certain classes of nonlinear switched systems. In particular, we formulate an analogue of Lyapunov's indirect method for [MATH] switched nonlinear systems and derive a new method for determining the existence of a bounded basin of attraction for a class of switched nonlinear systems.
tldr: This paper studies stability and bifurcations of planar switched linear and homogeneous systems, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper aims to provide necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform asymptotic stability under arbitrary switching in two-dimensional switched systems.
method: The authors use worst-case switching analysis and study codimension-one bifurcations of stability in switched linear systems.
result: They formulate an analogue of Lyapunov's indirect method for switched nonlinear systems and derive a method for determining bounded basins of attraction.
conclusion: The results contribute to control theory and nonlinear dynamics, but are unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Characterized Subgroups On The Unit Circle
authors: Rafal Filipow, Adam Kwela, Paolo Leonetti, Jacek Tryba
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an ideal [MATH] on [MATH], a subgroup [MATH] of the unit circle [MATH] is said to be [MATH]-characterized if there exists an integer sequence [MATH] such that $[MATH][MATH]^\star[MATH][MATH][MATH][MATH][MATH](a_n: n \in \omega)[MATH][MATH]_{a}()[MATH]=_{H,a}[MATH]P[MATH]\mathsf H_{a}()=[MATH](a)\in[MATH][MATH][MATH][MATH][MATH][MATH]_{(2^n)}()$ cannot be characterized. We use our results to answer several open problems posed in the literature.
tldr: This paper studies characterized subgroups of the unit circle defined by ideals on natural numbers, answering open problems in pure mathematics.
motivation: To characterize which subgroups of the unit circle can be described by integer sequences with respect to a given ideal, and to resolve open questions in the literature.
method: The authors introduce the notion of H-characterized subgroups and use combinatorial and set-theoretic techniques to analyze their properties.
result: They provide a complete characterization of H-characterized subgroups for certain ideals and show that some subgroups cannot be characterized.
conclusion: The results answer several open problems and advance the theory of characterized subgroups.

title: Designing Hierarchical Hub-and-Spoke Drone-Based Networks For Delivering Time-Sensitive Healthcare Items
authors: Sayed Hamid Hosseini Dolatabadi, Tanveer Hossain Bhuiyan, Bo Zeng, J. Tyler Kennedy, Brian O Neill
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Timely distribution of medical items (e.g., whole blood and vaccines) across regional healthcare networks often requires high-volume delivery operations from central facilities (e.g., blood banks) to intermediate regional hospitals, followed by rapid last-mile deliveries to points of injury. Traditional ground-based delivery systems often suffer from limited responsiveness (e.g., traffic congestion) and operational inefficiencies (e.g., blood waste). Leveraging aerial-drone-based delivery systems offers a promising solution for the fast and efficient delivery of time-sensitive medical items across regional healthcare networks. Therefore, we study a hierarchical hub-and-spoke drone-based network for delivering time-sensitive medical items with distinct release and due times to fixed and mobile delivery destinations. We consider a heterogeneous fleet of drones with distinct characteristics (e.g., cost, battery capacity, and speed) and different multi-trip delivery modes. We propose an efficient mixed-integer programming model for location/allocation of mobile delivery destinations, as well as routing and scheduling drones to minimize the total investment and operational costs of the drone delivery network while maintaining the delivery due times. We develop a customized exact solution method integrating problem-specific reformulations and dynamic cutting planes, as well as a fast heuristic algorithm by leveraging a simplified problem variant. Results based on a real-life case study of whole blood delivery data from Pendleton, Oregon, United States, and actual drone flight test data demonstrate that our exact and heuristic solution methods are 31 and 3,375 times faster, respectively, than the Gurobi solver. Results also show that allowing drones to perform multiple trips is 142.8% more cost-efficient than single trips.
tldr: This paper proposes a hierarchical drone-based delivery network for time-sensitive medical items, focusing on operational optimization.
motivation: Traditional ground-based delivery systems for medical items suffer from limited responsiveness and inefficiencies; drone-based systems offer a promising alternative.
method: A mixed-integer programming model is developed for location/allocation, routing, and scheduling of heterogeneous drones, solved with customized exact and heuristic methods.
result: The exact and heuristic methods are 31 and 3,375 times faster than Gurobi, and multi-trip drones are 142.8% more cost-efficient than single-trip.
conclusion: The proposed drone network design significantly improves cost-efficiency and timeliness for medical item delivery.

title: The Benjamini--Hochberg Procedure Can Fail To Control The Fdr For Correlated Two-Sided Gaussian Tests
authors: Edgar Dobriban
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Benjamini--Hochberg procedure can fail to control the false discovery rate (FDR) at its nominal level for correlated two-sided Gaussian [MATH]-values. We construct a factor model for which, at level [MATH], a rigorous interval-arithmetic certificate proves [MATH] for all sufficiently large numbers of hypotheses. This disproves a conjecture widely believed to be true for twenty years. Monte Carlo experiments are consistent with the theoretical result. The proof was obtained by GPT-5.6 Pro and carefully checked by the author.
tldr: This paper shows that the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure can fail to control the false discovery rate for correlated two-sided Gaussian tests, disproving a long-standing conjecture.
motivation: The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure is widely used for multiple testing, and it was believed to control FDR under positive dependence. This paper challenges that belief for correlated two-sided Gaussian tests.
method: The author constructs a factor model for p-values and uses rigorous interval-arithmetic certificates to prove that FDR exceeds the nominal level for large numbers of hypotheses.
result: The paper provides a counterexample where the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure fails to control FDR, disproving a conjecture held for twenty years.
conclusion: The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure is not universally valid for correlated two-sided Gaussian tests, and caution is needed in such settings.

title: A Log-Gaussian Scale-Space Limiter For Hybrid Continuum--Ballistic Gas Dynamics
authors: Bj{\o}rn Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a log-Gaussian scale-space limiter for hybrid continuum-ballistic gas dynamics. The method defines complementary continuum and ballistic weights as Gaussian cumulative probabilities in logarithmic Knudsen-number space. This construction gives a smooth numerical transition between Navier-Stokes-Fourier and kinetic/free-molecular fluxes and suppresses asymptotically invalid correction branches in the continuum and free-molecular limits. The limiter is incorporated into a conservative finite-volume interface flux by blending a Navier-Stokes-Fourier flux with a half-range Maxwellian kinetic flux. Numerical tests using one-dimensional DVM/BGK Fourier and Couette benchmarks show that rarefaction corrections improve macroscopic profiles relative to NSF. A parameter scan over the transition center and width gives a DVM/BGK-calibrated pair K0=0.03 and sigma=2.5, reducing the combined mean profile error by about 40% for the tested planar wall-bounded flows. The paper is intended as a proof-of-concept numerical method and calibration study.
tldr: This paper proposes a log-Gaussian scale-space limiter for hybrid continuum-ballistic gas dynamics, focusing on numerical methods for rarefied gas flows.
motivation: To improve the accuracy of hybrid continuum-ballistic simulations by ensuring a smooth transition between continuum and kinetic regimes and suppressing invalid correction branches.
method: The method defines complementary continuum and ballistic weights as Gaussian cumulative probabilities in logarithmic Knudsen-number space, blending Navier-Stokes-Fourier and kinetic fluxes in a conservative finite-volume scheme.
result: Numerical tests on 1D DVM/BGK benchmarks show that the limiter reduces combined mean profile error by about 40% with calibrated parameters K0=0.03 and sigma=2.5.
conclusion: The limiter provides a proof-of-concept numerical method for hybrid gas dynamics, but the paper is a calibration study without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Compact Coefficient Formulae For Logarithmic Tangent And Hyperbolic Integrals
authors: Luc Rams\`es Talla Waffo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give compact coefficient formulae for several hyperbolic integrals whose values are linear combinations of odd zeta values and even Dirichlet beta values. First, the coefficients occurring in shifted integrals with numerator \(\sinh((2k+1)x)\) are rewritten as single Chebyshev-arcsine coefficient extractions. For \(k=0\), these identities recover the zeta- and beta-type integrals studied by Kyrion, but replace recursive coefficients by the coefficients of powers of \(\arcsin x\). The same method also yields compact coefficient formulae for logarithmic tangent integrals. Finally, for \(m,n\geq1\), \(m\geq n\), and \(m+n\) even, we prove the general formula \[ \int_0^\inftyx}{x^{n+1}}\,dx = (-1)^{(m-n)/2} \sum_{p=\lceil n/2\rceil}^{(m+n)/2} {n} (2^{2p+1}-1) {\pi^{2p}} [u^{m+n-2p}](u\cot u)^{m+1}. \] In the diagonal case this gives the family \(\int_0^\infty(\tanh x/x)^N\,dx\) in a non-recursive cotangent coefficient form and makes the initial vanishing of the zeta expansion immediate.
tldr: The paper derives compact coefficient formulas for logarithmic tangent and hyperbolic integrals, expressing them in terms of zeta and Dirichlet beta values.
motivation: To simplify the coefficients in known integral identities and provide non-recursive expressions for certain families of integrals.
method: Uses Chebyshev-arcsine coefficient extractions and manipulations of series expansions to rewrite integrals involving hyperbolic and trigonometric functions.
result: Obtains closed-form coefficient formulas for shifted hyperbolic integrals and logarithmic tangent integrals, and a general formula for a family of integrals involving tanh(x)/x.
conclusion: The work provides a more compact and non-recursive representation of these integrals, but it is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Time-decoupling Scheme For Mixed-dimensional Poroelastic Models With Fractures
authors: Dongchun Tang, Linshuang He, Shuyu Sun, Minfu Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a locking-free decoupling method for a mixed-dimensional poroelasticity model with fractures. By introducing the total pressure, the fractured Biot system is reformulated as a four-field formulation involving the displacement, total pressure, matrix pressure, and fracture pressure. We establish an energy dissipation law for the continuous model, which shows its consistency with the second law of thermodynamics. Based on this formulation, a time-decoupled scheme is developed. At the initial time step, a fully coupled scheme is employed, while for subsequent time steps, the flow problem is solved first, followed by the mechanics problem. A stabilization term is incorporated into the mechanical equation to help reduce the restrictions imposed on the model parameters in the stability analysis. Energy stability is established for the semi-discrete scheme. For the spatial discretization, the displacement and total pressure are approximated by the Taylor--Hood element, while Lagrange finite elements are used for the matrix and fracture pressures. A fully discrete decoupled scheme is then constructed. Energy stability and error estimates are derived for the fully discrete scheme, and the method is shown to be locking-free. Numerical experiments are presented to support the theoretical results.
tldr: This paper proposes a numerical decoupling scheme for poroelastic models with fractures, focusing on computational efficiency and stability.
motivation: Efficient simulation of poroelasticity with fractures is important for geomechanics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: A time-decoupling scheme is developed using a four-field formulation with total pressure, and Taylor-Hood elements for spatial discretization.
result: Energy stability and error estimates are derived, and numerical experiments confirm the method is locking-free.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is effective for mixed-dimensional poroelastic models but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: An Adaptive Interior-point Method With Backtracking Line Search For Convex Constrained Optimization
authors: Oliver Hinder Fadi Hamad
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interior-point methods (IPMs) are widely adopted due to their high practical efficiency in solving linear, convex, and nonconvex optimization problems. For convex optimization, this performance is theoretically well-supported: there are strong complexity guarantees for self-concordant barrier setups , which cover linear and conic optimization. On the other hand, unconstrained convex optimization is well-studied. However, there is limited analysis of constrained convex optimization methods without the self-concordance assumption. We develop and analyze a regularized Newton method with line search applied to the log barrier function in the setting that the objective and constraints are thrice differentiable and have Lipschitz continuous first and second derivatives. Starting from a strictly feasible point, our method finds an [MATH]-approximately optimal solution in [MATH] iterations.
tldr: This paper proposes an adaptive interior-point method with backtracking line search for convex constrained optimization without self-concordance assumptions.
motivation: Interior-point methods are widely used but their theoretical guarantees for convex constrained optimization typically rely on self-concordance. This work aims to provide complexity guarantees under weaker smoothness assumptions.
method: The authors develop a regularized Newton method with line search applied to the log barrier function, assuming the objective and constraints are thrice differentiable with Lipschitz continuous first and second derivatives.
result: Starting from a strictly feasible point, the method finds an approximately optimal solution in O(1/ε) iterations.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a theoretical foundation for interior-point methods in convex constrained optimization beyond self-concordance, but the contribution is purely in optimization theory and not related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Metasurface Antenna-Enabled Leo Satellite Constellation Communications: Design And Optimization
authors: Wenfei Yao, Xiaoming Chen, Qi Wang, Qiao Qi, Ming Ying
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Next-generation low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations face critical bottlenecks in spectral efficiency and onboard hardware complexity. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces a novel architecture enabled by metasurface antennas (MAs) at the LEO satellites. In particular, MAs are metasurface-integrated feed antennas that perform high-precision beamforming directly in the wave domain, thereby effectively mitigating multi-user interference. Based on such an antenna architecture, a weighted sum rate (WSR) maximization problem is formulated by jointly optimizing the scheduling of feed antennas to terrestrial users (TUs) and the passive beamforming of the metasurface for system performance enhancement. To address this mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) challenge, an alternating optimization (AO)-based joint scheduling and beamforming algorithm is proposed. On the one hand, the proposed algorithm incorporates a polynomial-time minimum-cost maximum-flow (MCMF) method, which is dedicated to the optimal scheduling of feed antennas and TUs. On the other hand, it adopts a weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) method integrated with semidefinite relaxation (SDR) technique, which is tailored for metasurface beamforming design. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for MA-enabled LEO satellite constellation communications.
tldr: This paper proposes a metasurface antenna architecture for LEO satellite constellations to improve spectral efficiency and reduce hardware complexity.
motivation: Next-generation LEO satellite constellations face bottlenecks in spectral efficiency and onboard hardware complexity.
method: The authors formulate a weighted sum rate maximization problem and propose an alternating optimization algorithm combining minimum-cost maximum-flow scheduling and weighted minimum mean square error beamforming with semidefinite relaxation.
result: Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for MA-enabled LEO satellite constellation communications.
conclusion: The metasurface antenna architecture and joint optimization algorithm can effectively mitigate multi-user interference and enhance system performance.

title: An Adaptive Fourier Spectral Method For The Vlasov-Poisson System
authors: Giovanni Russo Seung Yeon Cho
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Numerical simulation of the Vlasov-Poisson system faces fundamental challenges due to phase-space filamentation. Standard spectral methods rely on artificial filtering to suppress errors, which inadvertently degrades physical structures and accuracy over time. This paper proposes a dynamically adaptive Fourier spectral method combined with high-order time splitting to overcome these limitations. To prevent filamentation-induced aliasing, we dynamically expand the wavenumber domain via adaptive zero-padding whenever spectral tail monitoring detects emerging fine-scale structures. Acting as an exact trigonometric interpolation, it inherently avoids the artificial smoothing of traditional filters, preserving mass and effectively maintaining the [MATH]-norm within the dynamically resolved scales. Numerical experiments on Landau damping and various instability problems validate the robustness of our scheme.
tldr: This paper presents an adaptive Fourier spectral method for numerically solving the Vlasov-Poisson system, focusing on computational plasma physics.
motivation: Standard spectral methods for the Vlasov-Poisson system suffer from filamentation-induced aliasing and require artificial filtering that degrades accuracy.
method: The method dynamically expands the wavenumber domain via adaptive zero-padding based on spectral tail monitoring, combined with high-order time splitting.
result: Numerical experiments on Landau damping and instability problems demonstrate robustness, preservation of mass, and effective norm conservation without artificial smoothing.
conclusion: The proposed adaptive scheme avoids traditional filtering and maintains accuracy over long-time simulations of the Vlasov-Poisson system.

title: SinCoTrap: A High-Order Locally Corrected Trapezoidal Rule For Periodic Singular Integrals In Arbitrary Dimensions
authors: Yingzhou Li Hengzhun Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present SinCoTrap (Singularity-Corrected Trapezoidal Rule), a high-order locally corrected trapezoidal method for periodic singular integrals in arbitrary dimension [MATH] with kernel [MATH], [MATH]. The scheme preserves the uniform tensor grid and modifies only a fixed, small stencil of weights near the singularity. For a correction order [MATH], the resulting quadrature attains the error rate [MATH]. We derive explicit, mesh-independent limiting correction weights via analytic continuation of a special generalization of the Riemann zeta function, yielding rapidly computable formulas that can be pretabulated for each [MATH]. This makes SinCoTrap both efficient in application and robust for high-order accuracy across a broad class of periodic singular integrals.
tldr: This paper presents a high-order numerical quadrature method for periodic singular integrals, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Periodic singular integrals arise in many areas of computational science, and existing methods lack high-order accuracy on uniform grids.
method: The method modifies a small stencil of weights near the singularity using analytic continuation of a generalized Riemann zeta function.
result: The quadrature achieves error rate O(h^p) for correction order p, with explicit mesh-independent weights.
conclusion: SinCoTrap provides an efficient and robust high-order scheme for periodic singular integrals in arbitrary dimensions.

title: A Fourier-Aware Projection-Based Periodic Parareal Method For Time-Periodic Problems
authors: Chenyi Tan, Yuncheng Xu, Yehao Zhang, Yangfeng Su
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-periodic problems arise when the desired solution is a periodic steady state rather than a transient trajectory. The periodic parareal algorithm with a periodic coarse problem (PP-PC) is a periodicity-preserving parallel-in-time approach for such problems. Projection-based correction can accelerate convergence of both parareal and PP-PC. In this paper, we propose a Fourier-aware construction of projection spaces and a new correction scheme to further accelerate the convergence of projection-based PP-PC. We develop a convergence analysis of projection-based PP-PC with the discrepancy-based correction scheme for general nonlinear time-periodic problems. For an arbitrary orthogonal projection, we derive a local one-step convergence estimate controlled by the unresolved error and explicit nonlinear contributions. A temporal Fourier decomposition bounds the unresolved error by a tail-leak quantity, which is small when dominant error modes are selected and their coefficients are captured by the projection space. For linear problems, the nonlinear contributions vanish, yielding a globally valid one-step tail-leak convergence estimate under weaker assumptions. Experiments on linear and nonlinear problems show that Fourier-aware PP-PC requires fewer outer iterations than Krylov-enhanced PP-PC. For the linear problems, the errors track the tail-leak bound. For the nonlinear problems, the experiments quantify the unresolved-error and explicit nonlinear contributions in the local one-step estimate and show that the evaluated tail-leak estimate follows the observed decay.
tldr: This paper proposes a Fourier-aware projection-based periodic parareal method for accelerating convergence in solving time-periodic problems.
motivation: Time-periodic problems arise in many scientific and engineering fields, and existing parallel-in-time methods like periodic parareal can be slow to converge.
method: The authors introduce a Fourier-aware construction of projection spaces and a new correction scheme to improve the convergence of projection-based periodic parareal, and provide a convergence analysis using temporal Fourier decomposition.
result: Experiments show that Fourier-aware PP-PC requires fewer outer iterations than Krylov-enhanced PP-PC, and the error tracks the tail-leak bound for linear problems.
conclusion: The proposed method accelerates convergence for time-periodic problems, but it is a numerical algorithm with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Path Reconstruction In Prehistoric Human Migration: An Adaptive Dijkstra's Algorithm Based On Wavelet Compression For Topographic Data
authors: Max Brockmann, Lena Perlberg, Angela Kunoth
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reconstruction of prehistoric migration routes requires the accurate evaluation of effective distances across complex topographies. Traditional Least-Cost Path Analyses (LCPA) using high-resolution elevation models often lead to dense computational grids, making algorithms like Dijkstra's prohibitively slow for large-scale archaeological modelling. In this paper, we present a novel approach using adaptive wavelet methods to dynamically compress topographic data. By retaining high resolution only in areas of high topographic complexity (e.g., mountain passes) and smoothing homogeneous regions, we significantly accelerate the Dijkstra algorithm without losing essential routing topology. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method using migration scenarios.
tldr: This paper applies wavelet compression to accelerate Dijkstra's algorithm for prehistoric migration route reconstruction.
motivation: Traditional least-cost path analysis on high-resolution elevation models is computationally expensive for large-scale archaeological modeling.
method: Adaptive wavelet methods dynamically compress topographic data, retaining high resolution only in complex areas and smoothing homogeneous regions.
result: The approach significantly accelerates Dijkstra's algorithm without losing essential routing topology.
conclusion: The method is effective for reconstructing prehistoric migration routes using topographic data.

title: Strong Order One-half Convergence Of A Coupled Tamed Euler--Peano Scheme For Reflected Stochastic Differential Equations With Super-linearly Growing Coefficients
authors: Ziheng Chen, Caiyun Hua, Meng Cai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study strong numerical approximations for reflected stochastic differential equations in possibly unbounded convex domains with super-linearly growing drift and diffusion coefficients. Under a coupled monotonicity condition and polynomial local Lipschitz assumptions, we first establish the well-posedness of the reflected SDE and derive uniform moment bounds for its solution. We then introduce a coupled tamed Euler--Peano scheme, in which the drift and the squared diffusion coefficient are tamed by a common factor and the resulting Euler--Peano path is corrected through the Skorokhod problem. This common taming factor preserves the drift--diffusion coercivity structure and yields uniform moment estimates for the numerical solution. We prove strong convergence of order [MATH] for both the constrained state process and the boundary regulator, thereby recovering the standard Euler-type strong order in this reflected setting. Numerical experiments for a reflected stochastic Ginzburg--Landau type system illustrate the constraint preservation of the scheme and support the theoretical convergence rate.
tldr: This paper studies strong numerical approximations for reflected stochastic differential equations with super-linearly growing coefficients, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper aims to develop efficient numerical schemes for reflected SDEs with super-linear growth, a topic in stochastic analysis.
method: A coupled tamed Euler–Peano scheme is introduced, where drift and diffusion are tamed by a common factor and the path is corrected via the Skorokhod problem.
result: Strong convergence of order one-half is proved for both the state process and the boundary regulator, recovering standard Euler-type strong order.
conclusion: The scheme preserves constraints and achieves the expected convergence rate, validated by numerical experiments on a reflected stochastic Ginzburg–Landau system.

title: A Mixed Precision Algorithm For The Matrix Square Root
authors: Bowen Gao, Daniel Kressner, Meiyue Shao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed precision algorithms can significantly enhance the performance of linear algebra solvers by leveraging increasingly powerful low precision hardware while recovering working precision accuracy through, for example, iterative refinement. In this paper, we propose a novel mixed precision algorithm for computing matrix square roots. Our algorithm combines a Schur decomposition approach in low precision with iterative refinement performed through an approximate Newton method. We perform a detailed convergence analysis of the approximate Newton method. For the special case of symmetric positive definite matrices, this analysis implies that one can recover full working precision accuracy under mild conditions. Numerical experiments on x86-64 architectures indicate that our algorithm frequently reduces execution time compared with a fixed working-precision Schur algorithm.
tldr: This paper proposes a mixed precision algorithm for computing matrix square roots using Schur decomposition and iterative refinement.
motivation: Mixed precision algorithms can leverage low precision hardware to improve performance while maintaining accuracy, and this work extends such techniques to matrix square root computation.
method: The algorithm combines a Schur decomposition in low precision with iterative refinement via an approximate Newton method; convergence analysis is provided.
result: Numerical experiments on x86-64 architectures show reduced execution time compared to a fixed working-precision Schur algorithm, with full accuracy recovered for symmetric positive definite matrices.
conclusion: The proposed mixed precision algorithm is effective for computing matrix square roots, offering performance gains without sacrificing accuracy.

title: Strongly Regular Banach Spaces With Big Weakly Open Subsets In The Unit Ball
authors: Abraham Rueda Zoca Gin\'es L\'opez-P\'erez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct, given [MATH], a Banach space [MATH] and a closed, convex and symmetric set [MATH] with the following properties: 1) [MATH] is strongly regular (henceforth, [MATH] is strongly regular). 2) Every non-empty relatively weakly-star open subset of [MATH] (the [MATH] closure of [MATH] in [MATH]) has radius one. In particular, every non-empty relatively weakly open subset of [MATH] has radius [MATH]. 3) Every non-empty relatively weakly open subset of [MATH] has diameter, at least, [MATH]. This constitutes an advance to the question whether there exists a strongly regular Banach spaces satisfying that every non-empty relatively weakly open subset of the unit ball has radius [MATH]. As a partial answer, we get that for every [MATH] there exists a strongly regular Banach spaces where weakly open subsets have radius, at least, [MATH].
tldr: This paper constructs Banach spaces with strongly regular properties and large weakly open subsets in the unit ball.
motivation: To investigate whether strongly regular Banach spaces can have weakly open subsets of the unit ball with radius one.
method: The authors construct a Banach space and a closed convex symmetric set satisfying specific regularity and openness conditions.
result: For any given epsilon, they construct a strongly regular Banach space where every non-empty relatively weakly open subset of the unit ball has radius at least 1-epsilon.
conclusion: The result advances the understanding of the geometry of Banach spaces, but has no connection to quantum information theory or the user's research interests.

title: On The Singularity Degree Of Shor Relaxations For 0-1 Programs
authors: Hao Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shor relaxations are standard tools for nonconvex quadratic optimization, but they may fail Slater's condition. The singularity degree quantifies this degeneracy by the number of facial-reduction steps needed to reach the minimal face. We determine how the constraints defining a binary feasible set affect this quantity. For every nonempty binary set defined by linear equations and inequalities, the Shor relaxation has singularity degree at most one. It is zero precisely when the linear programming (LP) relaxation contains a point in the open cube that strictly satisfies every inequality, and is one otherwise. As an algorithmic consequence of this characterization, Slater's condition can be restored by solving an LP rather than an auxiliary semidefinite program (SDP). In sharp contrast, for every [MATH], we construct a binary feasible set defined by quadratic equalities whose Shor relaxation has a positive semidefinite matrix variable of order [MATH] and singularity degree [MATH]. Thus, singularity degree is uniformly bounded in the linearly constrained case but can grow linearly with the matrix order when quadratic defining constraints are used.
tldr: This paper studies the singularity degree of Shor relaxations for 0-1 programs, a topic in optimization theory.
motivation: Shor relaxations are standard tools for nonconvex quadratic optimization but may fail Slater's condition; understanding the singularity degree helps quantify this degeneracy.
method: The author analyzes how constraints defining binary feasible sets affect the singularity degree, using facial reduction and constructing examples with linear and quadratic constraints.
result: For linearly constrained binary sets, the singularity degree is at most one; for quadratically constrained sets, it can grow linearly with the matrix order.
conclusion: The singularity degree is uniformly bounded in the linearly constrained case but can be large when quadratic constraints are present, with algorithmic implications for restoring Slater's condition.

title: Extension Of The Safeguarding Stepsize Interval In Adaptive Gradient Descent
authors: Nobuo Yamashita Saneatsu Kagawa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, inspired by the idea of Adaptive Gradient Descent (AdGD) by Malitsky and Mishchenko, we propose a method that adaptively provides a stepsize interval, which represents the condition for stepsizes ensuring global convergence. By projecting the Barzilai Borwein stepsize onto this interval, we can ensure global convergence and expect further acceleration of convergence. Furthermore, we propose enlarging the stepsize interval obtained by AdGD and show that global convergence can be guaranteed within this enlarged stepsize interval. This extension of the interval enables us to adopt the full Barzilai-Borwein (BB) stepsize more frequently. We report the results of numerical experiments on the stepsize that combines the proposed interval with the BB stepsize.
tldr: This paper proposes an extension of the safeguarding stepsize interval in adaptive gradient descent for convex optimization, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To improve convergence of gradient descent methods by adaptively determining stepsize intervals that ensure global convergence while allowing larger stepsizes like the Barzilai-Borwein stepsize.
method: The authors extend the stepsize interval from the Adaptive Gradient Descent (AdGD) method and prove global convergence within the enlarged interval, then combine it with the Barzilai-Borwein stepsize.
result: Numerical experiments show that the proposed method allows more frequent use of the full Barzilai-Borwein stepsize while maintaining global convergence.
conclusion: The extended stepsize interval provides a practical way to accelerate convergence in convex optimization without sacrificing convergence guarantees.

title: MindReader: Using LLMs To Encourage Memorable And Secure Password Replacement
authors: Anna Gerchanovsky, Lujo Bauer, Michael K. Reiter
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on the design and evaluation of MindReader, a tool that helps a user replace her password when she is required to do so. Left to their own devices, users tend to replace their previous passwords with predictable variations of the original ones. MindReader leverages LLMs to suggest password variations that are chosen to be easy for the user to remember but harder for an attacker to predict. To do this, MindReader infers the meaning behind original password components and then suggests semantically related (yet syntactically unrelated) components for the new password. In a user study, passwords created using MindReader were more secure than both replacement passwords created without using MindReader and original passwords. In particular, MindReader replacement passwords were harder to guess in an online attack than alternative replacement passwords even by an attacker with knowledge of the original password and full knowledge of the tool implementation. Passwords created with MindReader were also comparably memorable to alternative replacement passwords and original passwords, as measured by the ability of users to successfully log in a week after creating their password.
tldr: This paper presents MindReader, a tool that uses LLMs to help users create memorable and secure password replacements.
motivation: Users tend to create predictable password variations when required to change passwords, leading to security vulnerabilities.
method: MindReader infers the semantic meaning of original password components and suggests semantically related but syntactically different replacements using LLMs.
result: In a user study, MindReader-generated passwords were more resistant to online guessing attacks and comparably memorable to alternatives.
conclusion: LLMs can effectively assist in generating secure and memorable password replacements, improving password security without sacrificing usability.

title: MTD-Playground: An Attacker-Aware Evaluation Framework For Network Moving Target Defense
authors: Mohammad Farhad, Mohoshin Ara Tahera, Padam Jung Thapa, Shuvalaxmi Dass, Bhupendra Acharya
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moving Target Defense (MTD) has emerged as a proactive network cyber defense paradigm that increases attacker uncertainty through dynamic network reconfiguration techniques such as Software-Defined Networking (SDN)-enabled path randomization. However, existing evaluations remain fragmented due to inconsistent attacker assumptions, attack scenarios, and evaluation metrics, limiting reproducibility and deployment-oriented comparison. In this paper, we present MTD-Playground, an attacker-aware evaluation framework for benchmarking SDN-enabled path-randomization (PR) MTD techniques under realistic enterprise-style multi-stage attack scenarios. Beyond isolated security and performance metrics, MTD-Playground introduces a composite evaluation methodology for analyzing deployment effectiveness, mutation-interval trade-offs, and defender-attacker operational balance. Using periodic path randomization as a representative PR-MTD strategy, our evaluation shows that aggressive mutation intervals reduce attack success rates to 4-20% while increasing attack completion time to 160-311s across evaluated attack scenarios. At the same time, PR-MTD improves throughput by up to 30.9% and reduces internal-path latency without service interruption. Composite analysis further shows that shorter mutation intervals consistently achieve the highest deployment effectiveness and positive defender advantage. These results demonstrate that SDN-based PR-MTD can substantially disrupt multi-stage attack progression while remaining practically deployable in enterprise environments.
tldr: This paper presents an evaluation framework for network moving target defense, which is unrelated to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Existing evaluations of moving target defense techniques are fragmented due to inconsistent attacker assumptions and metrics, limiting reproducibility and deployment-oriented comparison.
method: The authors develop MTD-Playground, an attacker-aware framework that benchmarks SDN-enabled path-randomization MTD techniques under realistic multi-stage attack scenarios, using composite evaluation methodology.
result: Aggressive mutation intervals reduce attack success rates to 4-20% and increase attack completion time to 160-311s, while improving throughput by up to 30.9% and reducing latency.
conclusion: SDN-based path-randomization MTD can substantially disrupt multi-stage attacks while remaining practically deployable in enterprise environments.

title: Explaining Intrusion Alert Decisions Of Deep Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems For Security Analysts
authors: Vrizlynn L. L. Thing Ayush Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present EXP-SEC, a novel framework which can explain the intrusion detection decisions of DL-based NIDS (which lead to security alerts) in a way that is aligned with the domain knowledge of analysts working in Security Operations Center (SOC). We highlight the following features of our framework: (1) a forensic module that isolates the suspect packets/flow which likely caused an alert (2) an explanation module which can handle much more complex feature dependencies in network traffic than existing methods (features can be divided into overlapping groups and some groups are more important than others), and (3) a multi-stage mapping module which translates the feature/group-based explanations generated by explanation module to domain-specific explanations suitable for processing by security analysts. We evaluate EXP-SEC with state-of-the-art DL-based NIDS and our evaluation results show that EXP-SEC outperforms xNIDS (existing best performing explanation framework) in terms of group-level and overlap-aware explanation utility metrics while performing similarly in terms of conventional feature-level metrics such as descriptive accuracy, sparsity and stability. Moreover, taking the case of a state-of-the-art DL-based NIDS, we demonstrate the security analyst-friendly explanation format generated by EXP-SEC.
tldr: This paper presents a framework for explaining intrusion detection decisions of deep learning-based network intrusion detection systems to security analysts.
motivation: Security analysts need understandable explanations for alerts generated by DL-based NIDS to effectively respond to threats.
method: The EXP-SEC framework includes a forensic module to isolate suspect packets, an explanation module handling complex feature dependencies, and a multi-stage mapping module to translate explanations into domain-specific terms.
result: EXP-SEC outperforms existing methods in group-level and overlap-aware explanation utility metrics while performing similarly on conventional feature-level metrics.
conclusion: The framework provides security analyst-friendly explanations that align with their domain knowledge, improving the usability of DL-based NIDS.

title: Antiproof: Synthesizing Vulnerability Detectors And Proofs Of Exploitability
authors: Alon Shakevsky, Corban Villa, Ion Stoica, Raluca Ada Popa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discovering vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them requires high recall and reliable automatic validation, but existing approaches struggle to achieve both without prohibitive cost. We present Antiproof, an end-to-end vulnerability discovery system that combines neuro-symbolic detector synthesis for high-recall discovery with proof-of-exploitability oracles for automatic validation. Antiproof learns and iteratively refines static detectors from vulnerability datasets, then validates candidates by verifying whether executable proofs demonstrate concrete attacker capabilities. Evaluated on BountyBench and our curated KEVBench dataset, Antiproof detects 64 of 66 vulnerabilities, improving recall by more than 60 percentage points over static-analysis and neuro-symbolic baselines. In a scan of 50 widely deployed systems, Antiproof uncovered several hundred previously unknown vulnerabilities. We are responsibly disclosing all confirmed zero-days and have received 12 CVE assignments to date, including remote code execution vulnerabilities in Ray, SGLang, vLLM, and LiteLLM that could allow attackers to take over LLM training and inference systems.
tldr: Antiproof is a neuro-symbolic vulnerability discovery system that synthesizes static detectors and validates exploits, achieving high recall and uncovering zero-days in widely deployed systems.
motivation: Existing vulnerability discovery approaches struggle to achieve both high recall and reliable automatic validation without prohibitive cost.
method: Antiproof combines neuro-symbolic detector synthesis from vulnerability datasets with proof-of-exploitability oracles that verify executable proofs of concrete attacker capabilities.
result: Antiproof detects 64 of 66 vulnerabilities, improving recall by over 60 percentage points over baselines, and uncovered several hundred previously unknown vulnerabilities in 50 widely deployed systems, receiving 12 CVE assignments.
conclusion: Antiproof demonstrates an effective end-to-end approach for vulnerability discovery and validation, with practical impact on real-world systems.

title: Degree Lower Bounds For Torus Polynomials And $majority$ Vs $acc^0$
authors: Sundar Vishwanathan Vaibhav Krishan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The class [MATH] consists of Boolean functions that can be computed by constant-depth circuits of polynomial size with [MATH] and [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is a natural number. At the frontier of our understanding lies a widely believed conjecture asserting that [MATH] does not belong to [MATH]. A few years ago, Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett and Rao (ITCS 2019) introduced torus polynomial approximations as an approach towards this conjecture. Torus polynomials approximate Boolean functions when the fractional part of their value on Boolean points is close to half the value of the function. They reduced the conjecture that [MATH] to a conjecture concerning the non-existence of low degree torus polynomials that approximate [MATH]. We reduce the non-existence problem further, to a statement about finding feasible solutions for an infinite family of linear programs. The main advantage of this statement is that it allows for incremental progress, which means finding feasible solutions for successively larger collections of these programs. As an immediate first step, we find feasible solutions for a large class of these linear programs, leaving only a finite set for further consideration. Our method is inspired by the method of dual polynomials, which is used to study the approximate degree of Boolean functions. Using our method, we also propose a way to progress further. We prove several additional key results with the same method, including lower bounds for approximating the [MATH] function, lower bounds when the approximating polynomial is symmetric, showcasing the power of our machinery.
tldr: This paper studies degree lower bounds for torus polynomials approximating the majority function, aiming to prove that majority is not in ACC0.
motivation: The longstanding conjecture that majority is not in ACC0 is approached via torus polynomial approximations, reducing the problem to solving linear programs.
method: The authors reduce the non-existence of low-degree torus polynomials approximating majority to finding feasible solutions for an infinite family of linear programs, using a method inspired by dual polynomials.
result: They find feasible solutions for a large class of these linear programs, leaving only a finite set for further consideration, and prove lower bounds for approximating majority and symmetric polynomials.
conclusion: The work provides a new framework for attacking the majority vs. ACC0 problem and demonstrates its power through several key results.

title: Trust But Verify? Uncovering The Security Debt Of Autonomous Coding Agents
authors: A H M Nazmus Sakib, Dipayan Banik, Murtuza Jadliwala
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing adoption of autonomous coding agents accelerates software development but also introduces scoped security risks within high-impact file paths that can outpace traditional human review capacity. While prior research has primarily evaluated these systems in terms of functional correctness and productivity, this paper presents a large-scale empirical study using the AIDev dataset to systematically characterize security code smells in agent-generated pull requests (PRs). Through a combination of a validated LLM-as-a-judge framework and manual qualitative analysis, we identify and classify security misconfigurations across 16,112 file changes spanning 4,022 pull requests. Our results reveal that 38.9% of agent-generated PRs contain at least one security smell, with supply chain integrity issues accounting for 82.3% of all detected security smells. Furthermore, hard-coded credentials constitute 99.6% of all critical-severity security smells. Crucially, we find that human collaborators are responsible for introducing 67.6% of genuine leaked secrets within these agent-assisted workflows, while existing automated and human review processes fail to detect 81.1% of these credentials prior to integration. These findings highlight substantial security risks in agent-assisted software development workflows and suggest a potential reduction in developer vigilance. They also underscore the urgent need for context-aware security guardrails implemented directly at the point of human-AI collaboration.
tldr: This paper studies security code smells in pull requests generated by autonomous coding agents, finding that 38.9% contain security issues, mostly supply chain integrity problems and hard-coded credentials.
motivation: Autonomous coding agents are increasingly used but may introduce security risks that outpace human review. Prior work focused on functional correctness, not security.
method: Large-scale empirical study using the AIDev dataset, combining an LLM-as-a-judge framework and manual qualitative analysis to classify security smells across 16,112 file changes in 4,022 pull requests.
result: 38.9% of agent-generated PRs have at least one security smell; supply chain issues account for 82.3% of smells; hard-coded credentials are 99.6% of critical-severity smells; humans introduce 67.6% of leaked secrets, and 81.1% of credentials go undetected before integration.
conclusion: Agent-assisted workflows pose substantial security risks, and there is an urgent need for context-aware security guardrails at the point of human-AI collaboration.

title: When Binaries Talk Back: Representation-Confusion Attacks On LLM-Assisted Reverse Engineering
authors: Igor Santos-Grueiro
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-assisted reverse-engineering (RE) systems analyze strings, decompiler output, and tool reports derived from ttacker-controlled binaries. A binary can make data look like instructions or records from one origin look like independent evidence. We call such failures Representation-Confusion Attacks in Reverse Engineering (RARE): the pipeline promotes a correctly extracted observation to instruction authority, claim-validating evidence, or trusted analysis state without the authority or support that role requires. RARE-Bench measures these failures with behavior-checked clean and adversarial binaries. After an exploratory 11,520-call study, we test RARE-Guard's authorization and evidence controls on 20 new programs and two models. Without runtime controls, the models propose a planted unsafe action in 35/40 adversarial cases and 0/40 clean cases. When binary-derived content is shown only as data (Data-Only rendering), they still make 15 unsafe proposals. Tool Authorization denies all 15 and authorizes all 40 matched analyst requests.
