On identical report drafts, Support Gate validates 23/40 false claims by counting records from one origin separately. Provenance Gate groups those records before counting support, validates 0/40 false claims, and retains all 40 supported claims. We then instrument Ghidra, r2pipe, and angr on 16 further programs. In a preselected eight-program subset, no single-tool draft reaches Support Gate's validation threshold for the false claim. In fused drafts across all 16 programs, Support Gate validates 32/32 false claims. Provenance Gate prevents validation of all 32 and retains all 32 supported claims. A deterministic renderer prevents downgraded claims from reappearing in the final report. Binary-derived content may therefore guide analysis without gaining authority over tools, and views from several tools do not necessarily provide independent evidence.
tldr: This paper studies security vulnerabilities in LLM-assisted reverse engineering pipelines, specifically representation-confusion attacks where attacker-controlled binaries can mislead the analysis.
motivation: LLM-assisted reverse engineering systems are vulnerable to adversarial binaries that can cause the LLM to misinterpret data as instructions or evidence, leading to unsafe actions.
method: The authors introduce RARE-Bench to measure failures, and propose RARE-Guard with authorization and provenance controls. They test on 20 programs with two models, and instrument Ghidra, r2pipe, and angr on 16 programs.
result: Without controls, models propose unsafe actions in 35/40 adversarial cases; with controls, all unsafe proposals are blocked. Provenance Gate prevents false claims from being validated.
conclusion: Binary-derived content should be treated as data without authority, and multi-tool views do not provide independent evidence without provenance tracking.

title: Open-Source Intelligence For Code Provenance And The Security Patterns That Separate Human And Large-Language-Model Implementations Of Common Programming Tasks
authors: Mohammadreza Rashidi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developers now draw code from two very different sources, the accumulated human answers on sites such as Stack Overflow and the output of large language models. We ask two questions about that split. First, can the provenance of a code snippet be recovered from the code itself, and second, do the two sources differ in the security patterns they adopt for the same task. Using only open sources, a public gateway of open-weight language models and the public Stack Overflow API, we build a fully reproducible pipeline that collects real implementations of 31 security-sensitive programming tasks, among them OAuth with PKCE, JWT verification, password hashing, and SQL access, from 9 language models and from human answers, and scores every sample with deterministic security and style detectors. On 528 real samples we train a cross-validated classifier that recovers human versus model provenance with 93 percent accuracy against a 78 percent baseline, and a 7-way classifier that attributes a sample to the specific model that wrote it at 48 percent. We then report where the sources diverge on security, which patterns models adopt more often than the human corpus and which they inherit from it. Running the same tasks in Python, JavaScript, Go, and Java, we find the security divergence holds in every language while the provenance boundary is partly language-specific and does not transfer symmetrically between them. A vulnerability repair case study, in which models are handed insecure code and asked to fix it, finds a 77 percent repair rate across 21 seeds and 12 weakness classes, but a recurring partial-fix failure in which the model removes the insecure pattern without adding the correct defense. The pipeline is data driven, so any new task or language is added as a single specification entry, and a fail-closed checker re-derives every number in this paper from the stored data.
tldr: This paper uses open-source intelligence to distinguish code written by humans from that generated by large language models, and analyzes security pattern differences.
motivation: Developers increasingly use code from both human sources (e.g., Stack Overflow) and LLMs, raising questions about provenance and security implications.
method: The authors collect 528 code samples for 31 security-sensitive tasks from 9 LLMs and human answers, then train classifiers to identify provenance and compare security patterns.
result: A binary classifier achieves 93% accuracy in distinguishing human vs. model code, and a 7-way classifier attributes samples to specific models at 48% accuracy. Security divergences are found across languages.
conclusion: Code provenance can be reliably inferred from code itself, and LLMs exhibit distinct security patterns, including partial-fix failures in vulnerability repair.

title: VanillaBench: The Hidden Accuracy Cost Of Adversarial Robustness
authors: Niklas Bunzel
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adversarial robustness research has produced hundreds of defended models over the past decade, yet the literature almost universally reports robustness results in isolation: standard (clean) accuracy and adversarial accuracy of the robust model are shown, but the gap to the corresponding vanilla model is rarely quantified. We introduce VanillaBench, a systematic benchmark that makes this gap explicit. For every adversarially-trained model catalogued by RobustBench across four threat models, we compute the accuracy difference against multiple vanilla references from Papers with Code, computed over both all entries and no-extra-data entries, the best vanilla model as of the robust model's publication year, and an architecture-matched baseline. Across all 186 robust models, the mean delta clean relative to the best vanilla model ranges from -7.7 to -29.5 percentage points, and even the single most robust model per track still trails its temporal vanilla counterpart by 4.0-21.0 points. The architecture-matched comparison, which isolates the effect of adversarial training from architectural differences, reveals a mean gap of -3.5 to -17.5 points. Restricting this architecture-matched comparison to models whose vanilla accuracy is known for the exact same architecture, rather than approximated from a related one, narrows the gap to -4.0 to -14.0 points. These results demonstrate that the robustness-accuracy trade-off is substantially larger than what is typically conveyed by individual papers. This information is critical for practitioners and decision-makers. When deploying models in real-world settings, the accuracy cost of robustness directly affects business outcomes, yet current publications do not provide the vanilla baseline needed to assess it. We argue that future robustness evaluations should report vanilla-referenced accuracy gaps as a standard component.
tldr: This paper introduces VanillaBench, a benchmark that quantifies the accuracy cost of adversarial robustness by comparing robust models to vanilla baselines.
motivation: Adversarial robustness research often reports clean and adversarial accuracy without comparing to standard models, obscuring the true robustness-accuracy trade-off.
method: The authors compute accuracy differences between adversarially-trained models from RobustBench and multiple vanilla references from Papers with Code, including architecture-matched baselines.
result: Across 186 robust models, the mean clean accuracy gap relative to the best vanilla model ranges from -7.7 to -29.5 percentage points, and architecture-matched gaps are -3.5 to -17.5 points.
conclusion: The robustness-accuracy trade-off is substantially larger than typically conveyed, and future evaluations should report vanilla-referenced accuracy gaps.

title: How Agentic Is Agentic Commerce? A Population-Scale Measurement Of X402 Adoption And Authenticity
authors: Shengchen Ling, Yajin Zhou, Lei Wu, Cong Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are said to be forming an economy in which they pay, on their own, for the data, APIs, and compute they consume. x402, which settles a stablecoin payment on-chain for each purchase, is the most widely deployed protocol for this, and its hundreds of millions of settlements are read as proof that the economy has arrived. We show the count cannot be read as adoption: it is the one metric an interested party can manufacture almost for free, since the facilitator sponsors the gas and nothing on-chain marks who controls a payment. We give the first population-scale measurement of x402 on Base, supplemented with a coarser Solana census. Identifying settlements from their on-chain event and resolving the true payer through the meta-transaction layer, we sort each by what its trace can prove via a payment graph. Over a 280-day window Base carries 136{,}708{,}672 settlements worth \[MATH]187{,}861.35 that demonstrably reaches a nameable service and the \$20{,}258{,}746.09 (45.92\% of value) not provably manufactured. Finally, we resolve the count's manufacturable component, a coherent operator-driven economy, star-shaped, machine-timed, and gas-subsidized. Settlement count measures manufacturability, not adoption.
tldr: This paper measures the adoption of x402, an AI agent payment protocol, and finds that settlement counts are largely manufactured rather than indicative of genuine agentic commerce.
motivation: Claims of an AI agent economy rely on x402 settlement counts, but these may be inflated by manufactured transactions. The authors aim to measure true adoption and authenticity.
method: The authors perform a population-scale measurement of x402 on Base and Solana, identifying settlements via on-chain events and resolving the true payer through meta-transaction layers, then sorting by payment graph traceability.
result: Over 280 days, 136 million settlements worth $187,861 reached nameable services, while 45.92% of value was not provably manufactured. The count's manufacturable component is a coherent operator-driven economy.
conclusion: Settlement count measures manufacturability, not adoption; the purported AI agent economy is largely artificial.

title: Cycles In Liquid Democracy: A Game-Theoretic Justification
authors: Markus Brill, Rachael Colley, Anne-Marie George, Grzegorz Lisowski, Georgios Papasotiropoulos, Ulrike Schmidt-Kraepelin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A common criticism of liquid democracy within the relevant academic literature is that delegation cycles can occur, seemingly resulting in unused voting power. Yet, practitioners argue that delegation cycles are not only unproblematic but are even formed intentionally by participants. To bring theory closer to reality, we introduce a model that captures this strategic behavior under uncertainty. We study the existence, structure and quality of Nash equilibria, revealing that delegation cycles naturally emerge. To complement these findings, we perform computational experiments using best-response dynamics.
tldr: This paper studies delegation cycles in liquid democracy using game theory, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To reconcile the theoretical criticism of delegation cycles in liquid democracy with practitioners' view that they are unproblematic.
method: Introduces a game-theoretic model capturing strategic behavior under uncertainty, analyzes Nash equilibria, and performs computational experiments using best-response dynamics.
result: Delegation cycles naturally emerge in equilibrium, and their structure and quality are characterized.
conclusion: Delegation cycles are not necessarily problematic and can be a rational outcome of strategic behavior.

title: PVDetector: Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks On Purpose-Specific Llm Agents Through Policy-Violation Concept Analysis
authors: Junhui Wang, Hangtao Zhang, Zhirun Zheng, Li Zeng, Jiejun Xiao, Xi Luo, Lihua Yin, Saiqin Long
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as purpose-specific agents to handle domain-specific tasks such as customer service and code generation. These agents are expected to comply with not only generic safety guardrails but also purpose-specific restrictions tailored to their designated roles. Such additional restrictions enlarge the attack surface, particularly to prompt injection (PI) attacks. To defend against such attacks, existing detection methods primarily rely on analyzing input-output patterns, yet yield limited effectiveness. To address this limitation, we turn to analyzing the hidden activation space and discover that LLMs inherently retain latent policy-violation (PV) concepts when prompted with requests beyond their designated purpose. Particularly, PV concepts capture the semantics of conflicts between user queries and predefined restrictions, implicitly reflecting LLMs' intrinsic awareness of recognizing policy violations. Building on this insight, we propose PVDetector, a training-free framework that detects PI attacks during LLM inference by measuring hidden-state alignment with PV concepts, which are derived offline from the contrastive pairs of policy-violating and policy-compliant prompts. Experiments across multiple LLMs and datasets show that PVDetector achieves <1\% false negative rate with minimal auxiliary overhead, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Our code is available at [URL] .
tldr: This paper proposes a training-free framework to detect prompt injection attacks in LLM agents by analyzing hidden-state alignment with policy-violation concepts.
motivation: Existing detection methods rely on input-output patterns and have limited effectiveness against prompt injection attacks on purpose-specific LLM agents.
method: PVDetector measures hidden-state alignment with policy-violation concepts derived offline from contrastive pairs of policy-violating and policy-compliant prompts.
result: Experiments show PVDetector achieves <1% false negative rate with minimal auxiliary overhead, outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
conclusion: Analyzing hidden activation space for policy-violation concepts is an effective and efficient approach to detect prompt injection attacks.

title: Building Extensible Program Logics Through Effect Handlers
authors: Zichen Zhang, Simon Oddershede Gregersen, Joseph Tassarotti
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One strategy for reasoning about programs that have certain kinds of effects is to use program logics that provide specialized rules for reasoning about these effects. However, developing program logics requires skills that are distinct from those needed for using program logics, making the development of new logics challenging and less accessible. Moreover, when developing new logics, it can be difficult to reuse components from prior logics or combine support for different effects. In this paper, we propose an approach for operationally building extensible program logics based on effect handlers. Our starting point is an expressive program logic for reasoning about programs written in a pure, sequential language with support for effect handlers. Within this language, we implement handlers that model concurrency, distributed execution, and crash-recovery behavior. Then, by proving properties about these handlers, we extend the program logic and derive expressive rules for reasoning about these effects. In some cases, this approach leads to stronger reasoning rules than those found in prior program logics targeting these features. In addition, we develop a relational logic for proving contextual refinements between programs using effects. As with unary reasoning, handlers enable this relational logic to be developed in an extensible way.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to build extensible program logics using effect handlers, focusing on reasoning about concurrency, distributed execution, and crash recovery.
motivation: Developing program logics for different effects is challenging and not easily reusable; the authors aim to make logic development more accessible and modular.
method: They start with a program logic for a pure sequential language with effect handlers, then implement handlers that model various effects and prove properties about them to derive reasoning rules.
result: The approach yields stronger reasoning rules than prior logics for some features, and a relational logic for contextual refinements is also developed.
conclusion: Effect handlers provide a principled way to build extensible program logics, enabling reuse and combination of support for different effects.

title: Switched-Feed Pinching-Antenna Systems For Wideband Terahertz Communications
authors: Hans D. Schotten Wei Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pinching-antenna system (PASS) uses dielectric particles along a low-loss waveguide as reconfigurable passive radiators. Existing analyses conclude that the in-waveguide attenuation is negligible at low frequencies and millimeter wave bands; we show this fails at terahertz (THz), where realizable waveguide losses are dramatically larger. We develop a unified wideband THz-PASS propagation model integrating in-waveguide attenuation, atmospheric absorption, molecular re-radiation noise, and beam squint. Closed-form results follow: a band-averaged coherence factor; a cluster-center placement satisfying a band-edge SINR equalization condition; an associated placement-inversion threshold; and a proposed (SF-PASS) architecture in which a centrally located radio-frequency switch routes the signal among multiple waveguide segments, with a closed-form insertion-loss payoff threshold. Numerical evaluation at the best PASS-compatible THz operating point shows that SF-PASS substantially outperforms single-feed PASS in spectral efficiency and is competitive with a large-scale antenna array at much lower hardware costs.
tldr: This paper proposes a switched-feed pinching-antenna system for wideband terahertz communications, focusing on propagation modeling and hardware architecture.
motivation: Existing pinching-antenna models neglect significant waveguide losses at terahertz frequencies, limiting their applicability.
method: The authors develop a unified wideband propagation model incorporating in-waveguide attenuation, atmospheric absorption, molecular re-radiation noise, and beam squint, and propose a switched-feed architecture with multiple waveguide segments.
result: Closed-form expressions for coherence factor, cluster-center placement, and insertion-loss threshold are derived; numerical evaluation shows the switched-feed design outperforms single-feed systems and competes with large-scale arrays at lower cost.
conclusion: The proposed SF-PASS architecture is a promising low-cost solution for terahertz communications, but the work is purely in wireless communications engineering with no quantum information or thermodynamics content.

title: Barbed Similarity For The $\pi$-Calculus In Beluga: A Case Study In Coinductive Reasoning
authors: Lea Trogni (dipartimento Di Matematica, Universit\`a Degli Studi Di Milano, Italy), Gabriele Cecilia (school Of Computer,cyber Sciences, Augusta University, Augusta, USA), Alberto Momigliano
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formalize strong barbed similarity for the pi-calculus in the Beluga proof assistant, completing a line of work addressing the Concurrent Calculi Formalization Benchmark. By extending previous developments to include replication, we give a coinductive encoding of behavioral equivalence based on barbs and internal actions. Using Beluga's copattern-based coinduction, we obtain concise and compositional proofs, including compatibility properties and a context lemma characterizing barbed precongruence. The case study demonstrates the effectiveness of combining HOAS and coinductive reasoning for mechanizing concurrent calculi.
tldr: This paper formalizes strong barbed similarity for the pi-calculus in the Beluga proof assistant, focusing on coinductive reasoning for concurrent calculi.
motivation: The authors aim to complete the Concurrent Calculi Formalization Benchmark by mechanizing behavioral equivalence for the pi-calculus with replication.
method: They use Beluga's copattern-based coinduction and higher-order abstract syntax (HOAS) to encode barbed similarity and prove compatibility properties.
result: They obtain concise and compositional proofs, including a context lemma characterizing barbed precongruence.
conclusion: The case study demonstrates the effectiveness of combining HOAS and coinductive reasoning for mechanizing concurrent calculi.

title: Proof Theory And Dependent Type Theory: Distinct Foundations For Designing Proof Assistants
authors: Dale Miller
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper examines the foundational distinctions between proof theory and dependent type theory (DTT) in the design of interactive theorem provers. While several implemented systems are designed using the dependently typed {\lambda}-calculus to represent proofs, no major proof assistant is designed using modern structural proof theory, even though, as I will argue here, the sequent calculus offers a compelling alternative framework. Six specific topics are proposed where the proof-theoretic perspective is arguably superior to the DTT perspective. These topics include the separation of logic from proof structure, the strategic use of non-determinism in proof reconstruction, and the avoidance of complex typing-discipline issues such as universe levels and proof irrelevance. The final topic -- the treatment of bindings -- is further developed to demonstrate how a natural, intensional approach is achieved through the mobility of binders. This methodology is illustrated via the Abella theorem prover, which leverages lambda-tree syntax and the nabla-quantifier to provide an elegant environment for reasoning about the meta-theory of languages and logics involving complex binding.
tldr: This paper compares proof theory and dependent type theory as foundations for proof assistants, arguing for the superiority of sequent calculus.
motivation: To highlight the foundational distinctions between proof theory and dependent type theory in designing interactive theorem provers, and to argue that modern structural proof theory offers a compelling alternative.
method: The author examines six specific topics where proof-theoretic perspective is arguably superior, and illustrates the treatment of bindings using the Abella theorem prover.
result: The paper proposes that sequent calculus provides a better framework for separating logic from proof structure, using non-determinism, and handling bindings via lambda-tree syntax and nabla-quantifier.
conclusion: Proof theory, particularly the sequent calculus, offers a viable and in some aspects superior foundation for proof assistants compared to dependent type theory.

title: Anti-Unification Completeness Analysis In Pvs
authors: Mauricio Ayala-Rinc\'on (universidade Federal de Goi\'as), Thaynara Arielly de Lima (universidade Federal de Goi\'as), Maria J\'ulia Dias Lima (universidade de Bras\'ilia), Temur Kutsia (risc/johannes Kepler Universit\"at), Marcos Mercandeli-Rodrigues
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In syntactic anti-unification, one is concerned with finding the commonalities between terms, while (uniformly) abstracting their differences. The original goal of anti-unification development in the seventies was to automate inductive reasoning. Recent applications of anti-unification techniques include efficiently transforming sequential code into parallel code, detecting code clones, and preventing software failures. Previous work addressed the elements required to verify, in the Prototype Verification System (PVS), termination and soundness of a functional algorithm based on inference rules for syntactic anti-unification. This paper dissects all aspects required to formally establish the completeness of the rule-based algorithm, highlighting the significant differences in the formalizations of anti-unification and unification.
tldr: This paper presents a formal verification of completeness for a syntactic anti-unification algorithm in the PVS theorem prover.
motivation: To formally establish the completeness of a rule-based syntactic anti-unification algorithm, which is important for applications like code clone detection and parallel code transformation.
method: The authors dissect all aspects required to formally verify completeness using the Prototype Verification System (PVS), building on prior work on termination and soundness.
result: The paper highlights significant differences in formalizations between anti-unification and unification, and provides a complete formal proof of the algorithm's completeness.
conclusion: The work contributes to the formal foundations of anti-unification, enabling reliable use in software engineering and inductive reasoning.

title: Work-in-Progress: A Tactic For Pattern Matching In Autosubst
authors: Kathrin Stark Mathews George (heriot-Watt University Edinburgh)
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autosubst enables automatic equality-checking up to the sigma-calculus for assumption-free equalities, allowing users to avoid cumbersome reasoning about de Bruijn indices. While effective in many cases, this approach is inapplicable when matching against typing rules, reduction relations, or lemmas, requiring users to either phrase typing rules in a way that they work with Autosubst or even stating explicitly an alternative de Bruijn term. But even without beta-reduction, solutions of matching may not be unique. This paper presents a work-in-progress method for automatically pattern matching against assumptions, evaluated on standard case studies including the POPLMark and POPLMark Reloaded challenges.
tldr: This paper presents a work-in-progress method for automatic pattern matching in the Autosubst framework for de Bruijn indices, applied to the POPLMark challenges.
motivation: Autosubst automates equality-checking up to sigma-calculus but fails when matching against typing rules or reduction relations, requiring manual workarounds.
method: The authors propose a tactic for pattern matching against assumptions, evaluated on standard case studies including POPLMark and POPLMark Reloaded.
result: The method is still work-in-progress; no final results or benchmarks are reported.
conclusion: The approach aims to reduce manual effort in proof assistants, but the paper does not present a complete solution or evaluation.

title: A Strategy Language For Controlled Proof Search
authors: Romain Sidhoum (LIRMM, Univ. Montpellier, CNRS, Montpellier, France), Simon Robillard (LIRMM, Univ. Montpellier, CNRS, Montpellier, France), David Delahaye
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces the strategy language of Pgeon, a meta-prover with a clear separation between inference rules and proof search. We give the semantics of strategies as functions over proof states, and of the operators that are used to combine them, allowing for sequential composition, choice, repetition and interleaving of strategies. This language is designed to handle the challenge of fair proof search in semi-decidable logics, where simple depth-first exploration of the proof space is not guaranteed to achieve completeness. We showcase the expressiveness and effectiveness of the approach through case studies in first-order and modal logics.
tldr: This paper introduces a strategy language for controlled proof search in a meta-prover called Pgeon, focusing on fair proof search in semi-decidable logics.
motivation: To address the challenge of fair proof search in semi-decidable logics where simple depth-first exploration may not achieve completeness.
method: The authors define a strategy language with operators for sequential composition, choice, repetition, and interleaving, and give semantics as functions over proof states.
result: The approach is demonstrated through case studies in first-order and modal logics, showcasing expressiveness and effectiveness.
conclusion: The strategy language provides a flexible and fair proof search mechanism for meta-provers.

title: Pinching-Antenna-Assisted Terahertz Communications: Modeling And Benchmarking
authors: Hans D. Schotten Wei Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) employing dielectric waveguides have recently emerged as a promising flexible antenna architecture for high-frequency wireless communications. While prior work has focused primarily on millimeter-wave regimes, extending PASS to the terahertz (THz) band introduces distinct electromagnetic phenomena that invalidate conventional modeling assumptions. This paper develops the first analytical framework for THz-PASS that integrates in-waveguide propagation attenuation, evanescent coupling via coupled-mode theory, and THz-specific free-space effects including molecular absorption and its re-radiation noise. Using this model, we benchmark THz-PASS against conventional phased arrays under identical propagation scenarios. Our comparative evaluation reveals that THz-PASS achieves effective gains in spectral efficiency through proximity exploitation, making it particularly well-suited for confined and linear deployment topologies.
tldr: This paper develops an analytical framework for pinching antenna systems in the terahertz band, focusing on propagation modeling and benchmarking against phased arrays.
motivation: Extending pinching antenna systems to the terahertz band introduces new electromagnetic phenomena that require a dedicated modeling framework.
method: The authors integrate in-waveguide propagation attenuation, evanescent coupling via coupled-mode theory, and THz-specific free-space effects including molecular absorption and re-radiation noise into a unified analytical model.
result: The model shows that THz-PASS achieves effective gains in spectral efficiency through proximity exploitation, particularly in confined and linear deployment topologies.
conclusion: Pinching antenna systems are promising for terahertz communications in specific deployment scenarios, outperforming conventional phased arrays under certain conditions.

title: Superimposed Transmission For Cooperative Cellular And Cell-Free Massive Mimo Systems
authors: Hans D. Schotten Wei Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a superimposed transmission strategy for cooperative cellular and cell-free massive MIMO systems. By classifying users into near and far, the base station transmits an additional data symbol for each near user, superimposed on the signals from distributed access points. Successive interference cancellation is employed at near-user receivers to decode both symbols. The proposed strategy achieves the highest peak spectral efficiency while maintaining fairness at the cell edge, thereby outperforming all the existing network configurations in system capacity.
tldr: This paper proposes a superimposed transmission strategy for cooperative cellular and cell-free massive MIMO systems to improve spectral efficiency and fairness.
motivation: To enhance peak spectral efficiency and cell-edge fairness in massive MIMO systems by leveraging superimposed transmission and successive interference cancellation.
method: Users are classified into near and far; the base station transmits an additional data symbol for each near user, superimposed on signals from distributed access points, and near users employ successive interference cancellation.
result: The proposed strategy achieves the highest peak spectral efficiency while maintaining fairness at the cell edge, outperforming existing network configurations in system capacity.
conclusion: Superimposed transmission is an effective approach for improving performance in cooperative cellular and cell-free massive MIMO systems.

title: Bulkhead: Automated Semantic Detection And Remediation Of Container Escape Vulnerabilities
authors: Qiyuan Fan, Zhi Li, Junjie Li, Xiaofeng Wang, Bin Yuan, Deqing Zou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Filesystem isolation in container ecosystems is often weakened by cross-boundary path misresolution, causing path traversal (PaTra) vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities stem from insecure host-container interactions and have become increasingly pervasive as cloud systems mount shared resources, such as GPUs and agent workspaces, into containers to support AI workloads. Existing defenses remain inadequate. Kernel-level protections are intrusive, can destabilize system calls, and have therefore not been accepted into the Linux mainline. Detection methods rely on static rule matching or manual code auditing. Static rules can flag path-related functions but fail to capture the semantics needed to determine whether a host-container interaction exists, causing many false positives. Manual review requires domain expertise, making it costly, inefficient, and difficult to scale. To address this threat, we present Bulkhead, an automated framework that integrates large language models (LLMs) with formal methods for semantic vulnerability discovery and remediation. Bulkhead uses a multi-agent system to identify and repair PaTra vulnerabilities through multi-dimensional knowledge patterns generalized from known cases. It first applies high-risk functional patterns to locate entry points for cross-boundary interactions in containerized code, then uses call-chain patterns to recover the corresponding execution paths at suitable depth. The Detection pipeline analyzes these call chains against the application scenarios and threat model, identifying vulnerabilities such as missing security checks and TOCTOU flaws in cross-boundary interactions, and generating proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits for validation. These PoCs then guide patch generation. To ensure remediation correctness, the Patch pipeline performs assertion-driven verification using predefined model-checking templates.
tldr: This paper presents Bulkhead, an automated framework using LLMs and formal methods to detect and patch container escape vulnerabilities caused by path traversal.
motivation: Container escape vulnerabilities due to path traversal are increasingly common in cloud systems, but existing defenses are inadequate or intrusive.
method: Bulkhead uses a multi-agent LLM system to identify cross-boundary interactions, analyze call chains, detect vulnerabilities, generate PoC exploits, and produce verified patches using model-checking templates.
result: The framework automates semantic detection and remediation, reducing false positives and manual effort compared to static analysis and manual auditing.
conclusion: Bulkhead demonstrates an effective automated approach to securing containerized environments against path traversal vulnerabilities.

title: Silent Alarm: A J-Space Protocol For Comparing Danger Recognition Across Models And Quantization Levels
authors: Roman Prosvirnin, Victor Minchenkov, Alexey Soldatov, Vladimir Bashun
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jailbreak-robustness research typically evaluates safety through generated responses using an LLM-as-judge approach. Such evaluations, however, are sensitive to the benchmark's grading procedure and capture only observed behavior on a given set of attacks, without directly revealing the hidden fragility of the underlying safety mechanisms. This work proposes JADR (Jacobian Assessment of Danger Recognition), a protocol that measures a model's internal representation through Jacobian space (J-space, a recently proposed workspace of verbalizable concepts) before the first response token is generated. For every prompt and layer we record the top-k J-space tokens; these are grouped into six behavioral scenario axes and compared between a danger sample based on StrongREJECT and a safe control drawn from XSTest and OKTest. The method does not call on an external judge model: the computation runs entirely locally, on the activations of the model under evaluation, which lets us compare both different models against each other and modifications of a single model -- quantization and fine-tuning in particular -- on the same terms. The final comparison rests on the proposed SafetyAUC metric, complemented with bootstrap confidence intervals. The protocol is applied to six models (Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-Uncensored-4B, Qwen3-SafeRL-4B, Gemma 2 9B) across three weight-representation regimes -- BF16, INT8, and INT4 -- and checked against an independent behavioral evaluation with the StrongREJECT grader. The metric separates models with a strong versus a weak internal safety mechanism with statistical significance and captures substantively different effects across quantization regimes.
tldr: This paper proposes a protocol to evaluate jailbreak robustness of LLMs by analyzing internal representations in Jacobian space, without using an external judge model.
motivation: Current jailbreak-robustness evaluations rely on LLM-as-judge approaches that are sensitive to grading procedures and only capture observed behavior, not internal safety mechanism fragility.
method: The JADR protocol records top-k J-space tokens per prompt and layer, groups them into behavioral axes, and compares danger vs. safe prompts using the SafetyAUC metric with bootstrap confidence intervals.
result: The metric separates models with strong vs. weak internal safety mechanisms with statistical significance and captures different effects across quantization regimes (BF16, INT8, INT4).
conclusion: JADR provides a local, model-intrinsic evaluation of safety mechanisms that complements behavioral testing and reveals hidden fragilities.

title: Quiz Show Games: Searching With Bimodal Hiding
authors: Mingshi Yao, Thomas Lidbetter, Melike Baykal-G\"ursoy
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a quiz show game in which a contestant is presented with a sequence of questions. Each time the contestant answers a question correctly, she receives a prize and proceeds to the next question; the probability of answering each question correctly is given. If the contestant answers a question incorrectly, she receives a consolation prize and the game ends. The contestant's problem of determining the optimal order in which to answer questions, for known fixed parameters, is a classic one studied in Kadane (1969), and admits a simple index-based solution. We consider game-theoretic versions of this problem in which a game show host can choose how to allocate a fixed prize budget. Our models are motivated by operational search problems in national security involving reconnaissance missions and inspecting for evidence of nuclear enrichment, as well as certain scheduling problems. We study three variants of the game, corresponding to different ways in which the host can distribute the prize money. For the first variant, we provide complete closed-form solutions, including equilibrium strategies and the value of the game. We reduce the second variant to a game solved in the literature. For the third variant, we obtain partial results by analyzing a more general game with a geometric structure.
tldr: This paper studies game-theoretic variants of a quiz show game with bimodal hiding, applied to search and scheduling problems.
motivation: The authors aim to model operational search problems in national security, such as reconnaissance and nuclear enrichment inspection, as well as scheduling problems.
method: They analyze three variants of a quiz show game where a host allocates a prize budget, using game theory to find equilibrium strategies and the value of the game.
result: Complete closed-form solutions are provided for the first variant, the second is reduced to a known game, and partial results are obtained for the third via a more general geometric game.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into search and scheduling problems through a game-theoretic lens, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Searching for new hadrons and understanding charmonium decays provides insights into QCD, quark confinement, and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments, highlighting recent advances from BESIII.
result: The review summarizes current knowledge on hadron production in charm-meson pair systems and identifies BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: The field continues to advance with high-precision data from BESIII, contributing to the validation of QCD and the discovery of new hadrons.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its contributions to planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and highlight its scientific impact.
method: The paper is an editorial that reviews the observatory's achievements through three colloquia.
result: The editorial does not present new research results.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory had a revolutionary impact on multiple fields of science.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of the planetary radar system at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on observations of solar system bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo's radar system was the most sensitive of its kind, enabling detailed characterization of many solar system objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss is a major setback for the field.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo Observatory's contributions to radio astronomy.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo telescope and its impact on various fields of astronomy and atmospheric science.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific achievements from the telescope's operation.
result: Arecibo made major contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory was a transformative instrument in radio astronomy, and its collapse marked the end of an era.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere have led to significant insights in plasma physics and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
method: The paper is a colloquium review that synthesizes results from incoherent scatter radar, lidar, and optical measurements at Arecibo.
result: Key advances include understanding of ionospheric plasma processes, metal layers, and space weather effects.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace research, and its legacy continues to inform future studies.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm rain formation is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies using convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud processes under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can capture turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentration and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to address the precipitation bottleneck, but further work is needed to fully resolve the mechanisms.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae, focusing on detection and parameter estimation.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, and gravitational waves provide unique insights into the supernova engine and neutron star formation.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods using ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents the latest predictions for gravitational wave signals and outlines strategies for detection and parameter estimation in a multimessenger context.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from core collapse supernovae is a promising avenue for multimessenger astronomy, but the paper does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential challenge to the cosmological principle, using radio galaxy and quasar catalogs.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole anisotropy in the large-scale matter distribution with the cosmic microwave background dipole.
method: Analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to assess the compatibility of the matter dipole with the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, challenging the standard ΛCDM model.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require new physics beyond ΛCDM.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of astrophysical tests of self-interacting dark matter, focusing on dark matter halo dynamics and large-scale structure.
motivation: To understand the implications of self-interacting dark matter scenarios on galaxy formation and structure, and to summarize observational tests.
method: Review of theoretical models and astrophysical observations from galaxies to large-scale structures, within the Novel Probes Project framework.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interactions from various astrophysical probes.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable model, with ongoing and future observations expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, but recent experimental results have constrained its parameter space. The paper aims to survey the current status and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review theoretical developments and experimental constraints, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels at the HL-LHC.
result: The paper provides an overview of viable supersymmetric models and their expected signatures at the HL-LHC.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable in certain scenarios, and the HL-LHC will significantly extend the search reach.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and neutrino production.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: Updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic data.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive update on hydrogen-burning nuclear physics, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes advances over the past 20 years, focusing on key topics like turbulence and non-Newtonian effects.
result: Key advances in bubble dynamics are highlighted, but no quantum or information-theoretic results are presented.
conclusion: The paper provides insights for modeling two-phase flows, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. [Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.

title: Polarity And Fabrication Effects In Ar‐bombarded GaN
authors: Przemysław Jóźwik, Katharina Lorenz, Ewa Grzanka, Afonso Caçador, Joanna Matulewicz, Mikołaj Grabowski, Cyprian Mieszczyński, Renata Ratajczak, Andrzej Turos And Mike Leszczynski
abstract: This study investigates the response of various types of gallium nitride (GaN) crystals to ion irradiation, a process that is pertinent to the reliability of materials utilised in high-power electronic devices. Two types of c-oriented GaN, which were grown by ammonothermal method and hydride vapour phase epitaxy, were irradiated with 300 kV Ar ions. The influence of crystal polarity on the resulting damage was evaluated using ion channelling measurements supported by Monte Carlo simulations. The experimental data demonstrate significant disparities in the accumulation of disorder between the two materials. Ammonothermal GaN, despite its lower initial threading dislocation density, exhibits a faster increase in lattice disorder, consistent with the formation of point defects and small defect clusters. Hydride-grown GaN exhibits a distinct behaviour, with the channelling signal denoting the presence of extended defects, such as dislocation loops, that persist up to a fluence of 3 × 1015 cm−2. Signatures of point-defect-dominated disorder emerge only at even higher fluences. In the case of ammonothermal material, the polarity-related differences in disorder remain minor and are largely within the experimental uncertainties. By contrast, for hydride-grown GaN, the N-polar samples consistently exhibit higher damage levels than their Ga-polar counterparts. The significant increase in disorder observed at the highest fluence points to the initiation of plastic deformation, suggesting conditions that are conducive to substantial structural modifications.
tldr: This paper studies ion irradiation damage in GaN crystals, focusing on polarity and fabrication effects.
motivation: Understanding radiation damage in GaN is important for reliability of high-power electronic devices.
method: GaN samples grown by ammonothermal and HVPE methods were irradiated with Ar ions; damage was characterized by ion channelling and Monte Carlo simulations.
result: Ammonothermal GaN shows faster disorder accumulation via point defects, while HVPE GaN exhibits extended defects; polarity effects are minor in ammonothermal but significant in HVPE GaN.
conclusion: The study reveals material-dependent damage mechanisms and polarity effects, relevant for device design.

title: Phase-controlled Direct Laser Acceleration Enabled By Longitudinal Variation Of The Laser-driven Quasi-static Plasma Magnetic Field
authors: R Bhakta, I-L Yeh, K Tangtartharakul, L Willingale And A Arefiev
abstract: Direct laser acceleration (DLA) enables energy transfer from an ultra-high-intensity laser to plasma electrons and underpins many laser-driven particle and radiation-source concepts. A laser-driven azimuthal plasma magnetic field is a key player in this process: it confines energetic electrons, induces betatron oscillations, and makes possible a resonant interaction between the betatron motion and the laser field. While this betatron resonance can enhance electron energy gain, the gain itself generally drives frequency detuning and promotes largely reversible energy exchange that limits net acceleration. Here we show, using a test-electron model with prescribed fields, that a slow longitudinal increase of the quasi-static plasma magnetic field qualitatively changes DLA by introducing hysteresis in the ratio of the betatron frequency to the laser frequency experienced by the electron, so that this ratio depends on the prior evolution of the electron even at the same energy. This hysteresis enables phase control of the electron-laser energy exchange and suppresses the usual reversibility of DLA, allowing electrons to retain the acquired energy and sustain energy gain without intermittent losses.
tldr: This paper studies phase-controlled direct laser acceleration using longitudinal variation of a plasma magnetic field, a topic in plasma physics and laser-driven particle acceleration.
motivation: Direct laser acceleration (DLA) is important for laser-driven particle and radiation sources, but energy gain is limited by reversible energy exchange. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: Using a test-electron model with prescribed fields, they simulate the effect of a slowly increasing quasi-static plasma magnetic field on electron dynamics.
result: The longitudinal increase introduces hysteresis in the betatron-to-laser frequency ratio, enabling phase control and suppressing reversibility, allowing sustained energy gain.
conclusion: This approach could improve the efficiency of laser-driven accelerators and radiation sources.
